import dataclasses
import datetime
import logging
import typing
from io import BytesIO
from urllib.parse import urlparse
from zipfile import ZipFile

from packaging.metadata import Metadata
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import BuildTag, canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from .pkgmetadata import dist_info_name
from .request_session import session

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclasses.dataclass
class Cooldown:
    """Policy for rejecting recently-published package versions.

    bootstrap_time is fixed at construction so all resolutions in a single run
    share the same cutoff.
    """

    min_age: datetime.timedelta
    bootstrap_time: datetime.datetime = dataclasses.field(
        default_factory=lambda: datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
    )


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, order=True, slots=True, repr=False, kw_only=True)
class Candidate:
    name: str
    version: Version
    url: str
    is_sdist: bool | None = dataclasses.field(default=None)
    extras: tuple[str, ...] = dataclasses.field(default=(), compare=False)
    build_tag: BuildTag = dataclasses.field(default=(), compare=False)
    has_metadata: bool = dataclasses.field(default=False, compare=False)
    remote_tag: str | None = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False)
    remote_commit: str | None = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False)
    upload_time: datetime.datetime | None = dataclasses.field(
        default=None, compare=False
    )

    _metadata: Metadata | None = dataclasses.field(
        default=None, init=False, compare=False
    )
    _dependencies: list[Requirement] | None = dataclasses.field(
        default=None, init=False, compare=False
    )

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        # force normalized name
        object.__setattr__(self, "name", canonicalize_name(self.name))

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        if not self.extras:
            return f"<{self.name}=={self.version}>"
        return f"<{self.name}[{','.join(self.extras)}]=={self.version}>"

    @property
    def metadata_url(self) -> str | None:
        """PEP 658: metadata is available at {url}.metadata"""
        if self.has_metadata:
            return self.url + ".metadata"
        return None

    @property
    def metadata(self) -> Metadata:
        if self._metadata is None:
            if not self.has_metadata:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.url} does not have metadata")
            metadata = get_metadata_for_wheel(self.url, self.metadata_url)
            object.__setattr__(self, "_metadata", metadata)
        assert self._metadata
        return self._metadata

    def _get_dependencies(self) -> typing.Iterable[Requirement]:
        deps = self.metadata.requires_dist or []
        extras = self.extras if self.extras else [""]

        for r in deps:
            if r.marker is None:
                yield r
            else:
                for e in extras:
                    if r.marker.evaluate({"extra": e}):
                        yield r

    @property
    def dependencies(self) -> list[Requirement]:
        if self._dependencies is None:
            dependencies = list(self._get_dependencies())
            object.__setattr__(self, "_dependencies", dependencies)
        assert self._dependencies
        return self._dependencies

    @property
    def requires_python(self) -> str | None:
        spec = self.metadata.requires_python
        return str(spec) if spec is not None else None


def _wheel_metadata_path(url: str) -> str:
    """Return the wheel's root metadata path, ignoring URL query and fragment."""
    filename = urlparse(url).path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    return f"{dist_info_name(filename)}/METADATA"


def get_metadata_for_wheel(
    url: str, metadata_url: str | None = None, *, validate: bool = True
) -> Metadata:
    """Get metadata for a wheel, supporting PEP 658 metadata endpoints.

    Args:
        url: URL of the wheel file
        metadata_url: Optional URL of the metadata file (PEP 658)
        validate: Whether to validate metadata (default: True)

    Returns:
        Parsed metadata as a Metadata object
    """
    # Try PEP 658 metadata endpoint first if available
    if metadata_url:
        try:
            logger.debug(
                f"Attempting to fetch metadata from PEP 658 endpoint: {metadata_url}"
            )
            response = session.get(metadata_url)
            response.raise_for_status()

            # Parse metadata directly using packaging.metadata.Metadata
            # (avoiding circular import with dependencies module)
            metadata = Metadata.from_email(response.content, validate=validate)
            logger.debug(f"Successfully retrieved metadata via PEP 658 for {url}")
            return metadata

        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug(f"Failed to fetch PEP 658 metadata from {metadata_url}: {e}")
            logger.debug(
                "Falling back to downloading full wheel for metadata extraction"
            )

    # Fallback to existing method: download wheel and extract metadata
    logger.debug(f"Downloading full wheel to extract metadata: {url}")
    data = session.get(url).content
    with ZipFile(BytesIO(data)) as z:
        try:
            metadata_content = z.read(_wheel_metadata_path(url))
        except KeyError as err:
            raise ValueError(f"Could not find METADATA file in wheel: {url}") from err
        # Parse metadata directly using packaging.metadata.Metadata
        # (avoiding circular import with dependencies module)
        return Metadata.from_email(metadata_content, validate=validate)

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import logging
import os
import pathlib
import tempfile
import typing
import zipfile

import pyproject_hooks
import tomlkit
from packaging.metadata import Metadata
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name, parse_wheel_filename
from packaging.version import Version

from . import (
    build_environment,
    external_commands,
    overrides,
    packagesettings,
    requirements_file,
)
from .pkgmetadata import verbatim_dist_name

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from . import context

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

BUILD_SYSTEM_REQ_FILE_NAME = "build-system-requirements.txt"
BUILD_BACKEND_REQ_FILE_NAME = "build-backend-requirements.txt"
BUILD_SDIST_REQ_FILE_NAME = "build-sdist-requirements.txt"
INSTALL_REQ_FILE_NAME = "requirements.txt"

# marker for Fromager's stub PKG-INFO
STUB_PKG_INFO_SUMMARY = "Fromage stub PKG-INFO"


def get_build_system_dependencies(
    *,
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    version: Version | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path,
) -> set[Requirement]:
    logger.info(f"getting build system dependencies for {req} in {sdist_root_dir}")
    pbi = ctx.package_build_info(req)

    build_system_req_file = sdist_root_dir.parent / BUILD_SYSTEM_REQ_FILE_NAME
    if build_system_req_file.exists():
        logger.info(f"loading build system dependencies from {build_system_req_file}")
        return _read_requirements_file(build_system_req_file)

    logger.debug(
        f"file {build_system_req_file} does not exist, getting dependencies from hook"
    )
    orig_deps = overrides.find_and_invoke(
        req.name,
        "get_build_system_dependencies",
        default_get_build_system_dependencies,
        ctx=ctx,
        req=req,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        build_dir=pbi.build_dir(sdist_root_dir),
    )
    deps = _filter_requirements(req, orig_deps)

    _write_requirements_file(
        deps,
        build_system_req_file,
    )
    return deps


def _filter_requirements(
    req: Requirement,
    requirements: typing.Iterable[Requirement | str],
) -> set[Requirement]:
    requires = set()
    for r in requirements:
        if not isinstance(r, Requirement):
            r = Requirement(r)
        # Use the parent's extras for marker evaluation because PEP 508
        # markers like `extra == "foo"` refer to the parent's install extras.
        if requirements_file.evaluate_marker(req, r, req.extras):
            requires.add(r)
        else:
            logger.debug(
                f"evaluated {r} in the context of {req} and ignored because the environment marker does not match"
            )
    return requires


def default_get_build_system_dependencies(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path,
    build_dir: pathlib.Path,
) -> typing.Iterable[str]:
    """Get build system requirements

    Defaults to ``[build-system] requires`` from ``pyproject.toml``.
    """
    pyproject_toml = get_pyproject_contents(build_dir)
    return typing.cast(list[str], get_build_backend(pyproject_toml)["requires"])


def get_build_backend_dependencies(
    *,
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    version: Version | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path,
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment,
) -> set[Requirement]:
    logger.info(f"getting build backend dependencies for {req} in {sdist_root_dir}")
    pbi = ctx.package_build_info(req)

    build_backend_req_file = sdist_root_dir.parent / BUILD_BACKEND_REQ_FILE_NAME
    if build_backend_req_file.exists():
        logger.info(f"loading build backend dependencies from {build_backend_req_file}")
        return _read_requirements_file(build_backend_req_file)

    logger.debug(
        f"file {build_backend_req_file} does not exist, getting dependencies from hook"
    )
    extra_environ = packagesettings.get_extra_environ(
        ctx=ctx,
        req=req,
        version=version,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        build_env=build_env,
    )
    orig_deps = overrides.find_and_invoke(
        req.name,
        "get_build_backend_dependencies",
        default_get_build_backend_dependencies,
        ctx=ctx,
        req=req,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        build_dir=pbi.build_dir(sdist_root_dir),
        extra_environ=extra_environ,
        build_env=build_env,
    )
    deps = _filter_requirements(req, orig_deps)

    _write_requirements_file(
        deps,
        build_backend_req_file,
    )
    return deps


def default_get_build_backend_dependencies(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path,
    build_dir: pathlib.Path,
    extra_environ: dict[str, str],
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment,
) -> typing.Iterable[str]:
    """Get build backend dependencies

    Defaults to result of hook call
    :meth:`~pyproject_hooks.BuildBackendHookCaller.get_requires_for_build_wheel`
    """
    pbi = ctx.package_build_info(req)
    hook_caller = get_build_backend_hook_caller(
        ctx=ctx,
        req=req,
        build_dir=build_dir,
        override_environ=extra_environ,
        build_env=build_env,
    )
    return hook_caller.get_requires_for_build_wheel(
        config_settings=pbi.config_settings,
    )


def get_build_sdist_dependencies(
    *,
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    version: Version | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path,
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment,

        f"file {build_sdist_req_file} does not exist, getting dependencies from hook"

"""Derive PEP 376 distribution metadata directory names from wheel filenames."""

from packaging.utils import parse_wheel_filename


def verbatim_dist_name(wheel_filename: str) -> str:
    """Return the distribution name exactly as spelled in ``wheel_filename``.

    Raise ``packaging.utils.InvalidWheelFilename`` for an invalid wheel filename.
    """
    parse_wheel_filename(wheel_filename)
    return wheel_filename.split("-", 1)[0]


def dist_info_name(wheel_filename: str) -> str:
    """Return the dist-info directory name for ``wheel_filename``.

    Preserve the distribution name and version spelling, excluding any build tag.
    Raise ``packaging.utils.InvalidWheelFilename`` for an invalid wheel filename.
    """
    dist_name = verbatim_dist_name(wheel_filename)
    dist_version = wheel_filename.split("-", 2)[1]
    return f"{dist_name}-{dist_version}.dist-info"

@@ -0,0 +1,23 @@
+"""Derive PEP 376 distribution metadata directory names from wheel filenames."""
+
+from packaging.utils import parse_wheel_filename
+
+
+def verbatim_dist_name(wheel_filename: str) -> str:
+    """Return the distribution name exactly as spelled in ``wheel_filename``.
+
+    Raise ``packaging.utils.InvalidWheelFilename`` for an invalid wheel filename.
+    """
+    parse_wheel_filename(wheel_filename)
+    return wheel_filename.split("-", 1)[0]
+
+
+def dist_info_name(wheel_filename: str) -> str:
+    """Return the dist-info directory name for ``wheel_filename``.
+
+    Preserve the distribution name and version spelling, excluding any build tag.
+    Raise ``packaging.utils.InvalidWheelFilename`` for an invalid wheel filename.
+    """
+    dist_name = verbatim_dist_name(wheel_filename)
+    dist_version = wheel_filename.split("-", 2)[1]
+    return f"{dist_name}-{dist_version}.dist-info"

...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        return value.strip()\n    raise TypeError(f\"unsupported type {type(value)}: {value!r}\")\n\nEnvKey = typing.Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_validate_envkey)]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n| -- | -- |\n| Run tests | `hatch run test:test` |\n| Check code quality | `hatch run lint:check` |\n| Fix formatting | `hatch run lint:fix` |\n| Type checking | `hatch run mypy:check` |\n\n### Standards\n\n| Standard | Requirement |\n| -- | -- |\n| Type annotations | Required for every function |\n| Docstrings | Required on public APIs |\n| Tests | Required for new behavior |\n| Trailing whitespace | Forbidden |\n| File endings | Single newline |\n| Commit format | Conventional Commits |\n\n---\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for discussion or questions or design proposals.\n- File an issue with a minimal reproduction for bugs.\n- Ask for targeted feedback directly in your pull request.\n\n## Resources\n\n- [PEP 8 - Style Guide](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008/)\n- [PEP 484 - Type Hints](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0484/)\n- [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)\n- [pytest Documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [Ruff Documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)\n\n---\n\n**Thanks for {"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_9","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc 'cat /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/caveman/SKILL.md'","aggregated_output":"---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Test the basic integration of metadata URLs with candidates\n        candidate_with_metadata = Candidate(\n            name=\"test-package\",\n            version=Version(\"1.0.0\"),\n            url=\"https://example.com/test.whl\",\n            has_metadata=True,\n        )\n\n        candidate_without_metadata = Candidate(\n            name=\"test-package\",\n            version=Version(\"1.0.0\"),\n            url=\"https://example.com/test.whl\",\n        )\n\n        assert (\n            candidate_with_metadata.metadata_url\n            == \"https://example.com/test.whl.metadata\"\n        )\n\n        # Act & Assert\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=\"Could not find METADATA file\"):\n        dependencies._get_metadata_from_wheel(wheel_file)\n\n\ndef test_get_metadata_from_wheel_with_build_tag(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Test extracting metadata from a wheel with a build tag in the filename.\n\n    Wheel format: {distribution}-{version}-{build}-{python}-{abi}-{platform}.whl\n    The build tag is optional. parse_wheel_filename correctly separates the version\n    from the build tag, so the dist-info path is computed correctly.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Arrange: Create a wheel with a build tag (123)\n    wheel_file = tmp_path / \"mypkg-1.0.0-123-py3-none-any.whl\"\n    metadata_content = textwrap.dedent(\"\"\"\\\n        Metadata-Version: 2.1\n        Name: mypkg\n        Version: 1.0.0\n        Requires-Dist: requests\n    \"\"\")\n    with zipfile.ZipFile(wheel_file, \"w\") as zf:\n        # dist-info directory is {name}-{version}.dist-info (no build tag)\n        zf.writestr(\"mypkg-1.0.0.dist-info/METADATA\", metadata_content)\n        zf.writestr(\"mypkg-1.0.0.dist-info/WHEEL\", \"Wheel-Version: 1.0\")\n        zf.writestr(\"mypkg/__init__.py\", \"\")\n\n    # {"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_16","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc 'cat /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/caveman/SKILL.md'","aggregated_output":"---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

"""Tests for PEP 658 metadata support."""

import typing
from io import BytesIO
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
from zipfile import ZipFile

import pytest
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager.candidate import (
    Candidate,
    _wheel_metadata_path,
    get_metadata_for_wheel,
)
from fromager.pkgmetadata.pep376 import dist_info_name


class TestPEP658Support:
    """Test PEP 658 metadata support in fromager."""

    def test_candidate_with_metadata_url(self) -> None:
        """Test that Candidate can be created with a metadata URL."""
        candidate = Candidate(
            name="test-package",
            version=Version("1.0.0"),
            url="https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            has_metadata=True,
        )

        assert (
            candidate.metadata_url
            == "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata"
        )

    def test_candidate_without_metadata_url(self) -> None:
        """Test that Candidate works without metadata URL (legacy behavior)."""
        candidate = Candidate(
            name="test-package",
            version=Version("1.0.0"),
            url="https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
        )

        assert candidate.metadata_url is None

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_with_pep658_success(self, mock_session: typing.Any) -> None:
        """Test successful metadata retrieval via PEP 658 endpoint."""
        # Mock the metadata response
        mock_response = Mock()
        mock_response.content = b"""Metadata-Version: 2.1
Name: test-package
Version: 1.0.0
Summary: A test package
Requires-Dist: requests >= 2.0.0
"""
        mock_response.raise_for_status.return_value = None
        mock_session.get.return_value = mock_response

        wheel_url = "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"
        metadata_url = (
            "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata"
        )

        metadata = get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url)

        # Verify the metadata was parsed correctly
        assert metadata.name == "test-package"
        assert str(metadata.version) == "1.0.0"
        assert metadata.summary == "A test package"
        assert metadata.requires_dist is not None
        assert any(str(req) == "requests>=2.0.0" for req in metadata.requires_dist)

        # Verify only the metadata URL was called, not the wheel URL
        mock_session.get.assert_called_once_with(metadata_url)

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_pep658_fallback_behavior(
        self, mock_session: typing.Any
    ) -> None:
        """Test that PEP 658 is tried first, then falls back to wheel download."""
        # Mock that metadata URL fails, then wheel URL succeeds
        responses = []

        def side_effect(url: str) -> typing.Any:
            if url.endswith(".metadata"):
                # First call - metadata request fails
                mock_response = Mock()
                mock_response.raise_for_status.side_effect = Exception("404 Not Found")
                responses.append(("metadata", url))
                return mock_response
            else:
                # Second call - wheel request
                responses.append(("wheel", url))
                raise Exception("Wheel parsing intentionally mocked to fail")

        mock_session.get.side_effect = side_effect

        wheel_url = "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"
        metadata_url = (
            "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata"
        )

        # This should raise an exception during wheel parsing, but we can verify the order
        try:
            get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url)
        except Exception:
            pass  # Expected to fail during wheel parsing mock

        # Verify that both URLs were called in the correct order
        assert len(responses) == 2
        assert responses[0] == ("metadata", metadata_url)
        assert responses[1] == ("wheel", wheel_url)
        assert mock_session.get.call_count == 2

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_without_pep658_behavior(
        self, mock_session: typing.Any
    ) -> None:
        """Test that without PEP 658 metadata URL, only wheel URL is called."""
        # Mock wheel request
        responses = []

        def side_effect(url: str) -> typing.Any:
            responses.append(("wheel", url))
            raise Exception("Wheel parsing intentionally mocked to fail")

        mock_session.get.side_effect = side_effect

        wheel_url = "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"

        # This should raise an exception during wheel parsing, but we can verify the behavior
        try:
            get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url=None)
        except Exception:
            pass  # Expected to fail during wheel parsing mock

        # Verify that only the wheel URL was called
        assert len(responses) == 1
        assert responses[0] == ("wheel", wheel_url)
        mock_session.get.assert_called_once_with(wheel_url)

    def test_candidate_repr_with_metadata_url(self) -> None:
        """Test that Candidate representation includes metadata URL info."""
        candidate = Candidate(
            name="test-package",
            version=Version("1.0.0"),
            url="https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            has_metadata=True,
        )

        # The candidate should have the metadata URL attribute
        assert hasattr(candidate, "metadata_url")
        assert (
            candidate.metadata_url
            == "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata"
        )

    def test_metadata_url_construction(self) -> None:
        """Test that metadata URLs are constructed correctly."""
        base_url = (
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-package/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"
        )
        expected_metadata_url = base_url + ".metadata"

        # This tests the expected pattern for PEP 658 metadata URLs
        assert expected_metadata_url.endswith(".whl.metadata")
        assert expected_metadata_url.startswith("https://")

    def test_pep658_integration_with_resolver(self) -> None:
        """Test that PEP 658 metadata URLs are properly handled by the candidate system."""
        # Test the basic integration of metadata URLs with candidates
        candidate_with_metadata = Candidate(
            name="test-package",
            version=Version("1.0.0"),
            url="https://example.com/test.whl",
            has_metadata=True,
        )

        candidate_without_metadata = Candidate(
            name="test-package",
            version=Version("1.0.0"),
            url="https://example.com/test.whl",
        )

        assert (
            candidate_with_metadata.metadata_url
            == "https://example.com/test.whl.metadata"
        )

        # Verify PEP 658 metadata URL handling
        assert (
            candidate_with_metadata.metadata_url
            == "https://example.com/test.whl.metadata"
        )
        assert candidate_without_metadata.metadata_url is None

        # Both should have the same basic properties
        assert candidate_with_metadata.name == candidate_without_metadata.name
        assert candidate_with_metadata.version == candidate_without_metadata.version

from collections.abc import Callable

import pytest
from packaging.metadata import Metadata, RawMetadata
from packaging.utils import InvalidWheelFilename

from fromager.pkgmetadata import (
    dist_info_name,
    license_from_metadata,
    license_from_metadata_values,
    normalize_project_urls,
    project_urls_from_metadata,
    verbatim_dist_name,
)

URL = "https://home.test"
URL2 = "https://other.test"


def md(
    license_expression: str | None = None,
    license: str | None = None,
    classifiers: list[str] | None = None,
    home_page: str | None = None,
    download_url: str | None = None,
    project_urls: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> Metadata:
    raw = RawMetadata(
        metadata_version="2.4",
        name="test",
        version="1.0",
    )
    if license_expression is not None:
        raw["license_expression"] = license_expression
    if license is not None:
        raw["license"] = license
    if classifiers is not None:
        raw["classifiers"] = classifiers
    if home_page is not None:
        raw["home_page"] = home_page
    if download_url is not None:
        raw["download_url"] = download_url
    if project_urls is not None:
        raw["project_urls"] = project_urls
    return Metadata.from_raw(raw)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ["urls", "expected"],
    [
        [{}, []],
        [{"Home-Page": URL}, [("homepage", URL)]],
        [
            {"Home-Page": URL, "homepage": URL2},
            [("homepage", URL), ("homepage", URL2)],
        ],
        [{"Home-Page": URL, "homepage": URL}, [("homepage", URL)]],
        [{"What's New?": URL}, [("changelog", URL)]],
        [{"Git Hub": URL}, [("source", URL)]],
        [{"Other Stuff": URL}, [("Other Stuff", URL)]],
    ],
)
def test_normalize_project_urls(
    urls: dict[str, str], expected: list[tuple[str, str]]
) -> None:
    assert normalize_project_urls(list(urls.items())) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ["metadata", "expected"],
    [
        [md(), []],
        [md(home_page=URL), [("homepage", URL)]],
        [
            md(home_page=URL, project_urls={"homepage": URL2}),
            [("homepage", URL), ("homepage", URL2)],
        ],
    ],
)
def test_project_urls_from_metadata(
    metadata: Metadata, expected: list[tuple[str, str]]
) -> None:
    assert project_urls_from_metadata(metadata) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ["metadata", "expected"],
    [
        [md("MIT AND MIT or MIT"), "MIT"],
        [md(license="MIT License"), "MIT"],
        [md(license="MIT and PSF-2.0"), "MIT AND PSF-2.0"],
        [md(license="BSD 3-Clause License"), "BSD-3-Clause"],
        [md(classifiers=["License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License"]), "MIT"],
        [
            md(
                classifiers=[
                    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
                    "License :: OSI Approved :: Python Software Foundation License",
                ]
            ),
            "MIT AND PSF-2.0",
        ],
    ],
)
def test_license_from_metadata(metadata: Metadata, expected: str) -> None:
    expr = license_from_metadata(metadata)
    assert str(expr.simplify()) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ["license_expression", "license", "classifiers"],
    [
        (None, None, None),
        (None, "invalid", None),
        (None, None, ["License :: OSI Approved :: BSD License"]),
    ],
)
def test_license_from_metadata_errors(
    license_expression: str | None,
    license: str | None,
    classifiers: list[str] | None,
) -> None:
    with pytest.raises((ValueError, ExceptionGroup)):
        license_from_metadata_values(
            license_expression=license_expression,
            license_text=license,
            classifiers=classifiers,
        )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ["wheel_filename", "dist_name", "dist_info"],
    [
        ("mypkg-1.0-py3-none-any.whl", "mypkg", "mypkg-1.0.dist-info"),
        (
            "MarkupSafe-1.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "MarkupSafe",
            "MarkupSafe-1.0.dist-info",
        ),
        (
            "oslo.messaging-1.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "oslo.messaging",
            "oslo.messaging-1.0.dist-info",
        ),
        ("my_pkg-1.0-py3-none-any.whl", "my_pkg", "my_pkg-1.0.dist-info"),
        (
            "MarkupSafe-1.0RC1-123-py3-none-any.whl",
            "MarkupSafe",
            "MarkupSafe-1.0RC1.dist-info",
        ),
        (
            "mypkg-01.002.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "mypkg",
            "mypkg-01.002.0.dist-info",
        ),
        (
            "mypkg-1.0+LOCAL-py3-none-any.whl",
            "mypkg",
            "mypkg-1.0+LOCAL.dist-info",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_wheel_metadata_names(
    wheel_filename: str, dist_name: str, dist_info: str
) -> None:
    """Preserve wheel name and version spelling without the build tag."""
    assert verbatim_dist_name(wheel_filename) == dist_name
    assert dist_info_name(wheel_filename) == dist_info


@pytest.mark.parametrize("helper", [verbatim_dist_name, dist_info_name])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "wheel_filename",
    [
        "",
        "mypkg-1.0.tar.gz",
        "mypkg-1.0-py3-none-any.zip",
        "mypkg-1.0.whl",
        "my-pkg-1.0-py3-none-any.whl",
        "my__pkg-1.0-py3-none-any.whl",
        "mypkg-invalid-py3-none-any.whl",
        "mypkg-1.0-invalid-py3-none-any.whl",
    ],
)
def test_wheel_metadata_names_invalid_filename(
    helper: Callable[[str], str], wheel_filename: str
) -> None:
    """Validate the entire wheel filename before extracting its components."""
    with pytest.raises(InvalidWheelFilename):
        helper(wheel_filename)

FROMAGER_BUILD_SETTINGS = "fromager-build-settings"
FROMAGER_ELF_PROVIDES = "fromager-elf-provides.txt"
FROMAGER_ELF_REQUIRES = "fromager-elf-requires.txt"
FROMAGER_BUILD_REQ_PREFIX = "fromager"


def _log_existing_sboms(
    req: Requirement,
    dist_info_dir: pathlib.Path,
) -> None:
    """Log any existing SBOM files found in the wheel's .dist-info/sboms/ directory."""
    sboms_dir = dist_info_dir / "sboms"
    if not sboms_dir.is_dir():
        return
    sbom_files = sorted(sboms_dir.iterdir())
    if sbom_files:
        names = [f.name for f in sbom_files]
        logger.info(
            "%s: found existing SBOM files in wheel: %s",
            req.name,
            ", ".join(names),
        )


def _extra_metadata_elfdeps(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    wheel_root_dir: pathlib.Path,
    dist_info_dir: pathlib.Path,
) -> typing.Iterable[elfdeps.ELFInfo]:
    """Analyze a wheel's ELF dependencies and add info files

    Logs and returns library dependencies and library provides. Writes
    requirements to dist-info.
    """
    # mapping of required libraries to list of versions
    requires: set[elfdeps.SOInfo] = set()
    provides: set[elfdeps.SOInfo] = set()
    runpaths: set[str] = set()
    elfinfos: list[elfdeps.ELFInfo] = []

    settings = elfdeps.ELFAnalyzeSettings(filter_soname=True)
    for info in elfdeps.analyze_dirtree(wheel_root_dir, settings=settings):
        if info.filename is not None:
            relname = str(info.filename.relative_to(wheel_root_dir))
        else:
            relname = "n/a"
        logger.debug(
            f"{relname} ({info.soname}) "
            f"requires {sorted(info.requires)}, "
            f"provides {sorted(info.provides)}"
        )
        provides.update(info.provides)
        requires.update(info.requires)
        if info.runpath is not None:
            runpaths.update(info.runpath)
        elfinfos.append(info)

    # Don't list provided names as requirements
    requires = requires.difference(provides)

    if requires:
        reqmap: dict[str, list[str]] = collections.defaultdict(list)
        for r in requires:
            reqmap[r.soname].append(r.version)

        names = sorted(
            name for name in reqmap if not name.startswith(("ld-linux", "rtld"))
        )
        logger.info("Requires libraries: %s", ", ".join(names))
        for name, versions in sorted(reqmap.items()):
            logger.debug(
                "Requires %s(%s)",
                name,
                ", ".join(v for v in versions if v),
            )

        requires_file = dist_info_dir / FROMAGER_ELF_REQUIRES
        with requires_file.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for soinfo in sorted(requires):
                f.write(f"{soinfo}\n")

    if provides:
        names = sorted(p.soname for p in provides)
        logger.info("Provides libraries: %s", ", ".join(names))

        provides_file = dist_info_dir / FROMAGER_ELF_PROVIDES
        with provides_file.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for soinfo in sorted(provides):
                f.write(f"{soinfo}\n")

    if runpaths:
        logger.info("Libraries have runpath: %s", " ".join(sorted(runpaths)))

    return elfinfos


def extract_info_from_wheel_file(
    req: Requirement, wheel_file: pathlib.Path
) -> tuple[str, Version, BuildTag, frozenset[Tag]]:
    """Extract metadata from a wheel filename.

    Returns the **verbatim** dist name (not normalized) because the
    dist-info directory inside the wheel uses the original casing
    (e.g. ``MarkupSafe``, not ``markupsafe``). Uses ``parse_wheel_filename``
    for validation and to extract version, build tag, and platform tags.
    """
    # parse_wheel_filename normalizes the dist name, however the dist-info
    # directory uses the verbatim distribution name from the wheel file.
    # Packages with upper case names like "MarkupSafe" are affected.
    dist_name_normalized, dist_version, build_tag, wheel_tags = parse_wheel_filename(
        wheel_file.name
    )
    dist_name = verbatim_dist_name(wheel_file.name)
    if dist_name_normalized != canonicalize_name(dist_name):
        # sanity check, should never fail
        raise ValueError(f"{dist_name_normalized} does not match {dist_name}")
    return (dist_name, dist_version, build_tag, wheel_tags)


def default_add_extra_metadata_to_wheels(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,

    extra_environ: dict[str, str],
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path,
    dist_info_dir: pathlib.Path,
) -> dict[str, typing.Any]:
    """Default implementation returns empty dict - no extra metadata."""
    return {}

  wheel. Or better: parse the URL, split the name, and use

  `{dist_name}-{dist_version}.dist-info/METADATA`.

import dataclasses
import datetime
import logging
import typing
from io import BytesIO
from urllib.parse import unquote, urlparse
from zipfile import ZipFile

from packaging.metadata import Metadata
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import BuildTag, canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from .request_session import session

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclasses.dataclass
class Cooldown:
    """Policy for rejecting recently-published package versions.

    bootstrap_time is fixed at construction so all resolutions in a single run
    share the same cutoff.
    """

    min_age: datetime.timedelta
    bootstrap_time: datetime.datetime = dataclasses.field(
        default_factory=lambda: datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
    )


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, order=True, slots=True, repr=False, kw_only=True)
class Candidate:
    name: str
    version: Version
    url: str
    is_sdist: bool | None = dataclasses.field(default=None)
    extras: tuple[str, ...] = dataclasses.field(default=(), compare=False)
    build_tag: BuildTag = dataclasses.field(default=(), compare=False)
    has_metadata: bool = dataclasses.field(default=False, compare=False)
    remote_tag: str | None = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False)
    remote_commit: str | None = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False)
    upload_time: datetime.datetime | None = dataclasses.field(
        default=None, compare=False
    )

    _metadata: Metadata | None = dataclasses.field(
        default=None, init=False, compare=False
    )
    _dependencies: list[Requirement] | None = dataclasses.field(
        default=None, init=False, compare=False
    )

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        # force normalized name
        object.__setattr__(self, "name", canonicalize_name(self.name))

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        if not self.extras:
            return f"<{self.name}=={self.version}>"
        return f"<{self.name}[{','.join(self.extras)}]=={self.version}>"

    @property
    def metadata_url(self) -> str | None:
        """PEP 658: metadata is available at {url}.metadata"""
        if self.has_metadata:
            return self.url + ".metadata"
        return None

    @property
    def metadata(self) -> Metadata:
        if self._metadata is None:
            if not self.has_metadata:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.url} does not have metadata")
            metadata = get_metadata_for_wheel(self.url, self.metadata_url)
            object.__setattr__(self, "_metadata", metadata)
        assert self._metadata
        return self._metadata

    def _get_dependencies(self) -> typing.Iterable[Requirement]:
        deps = self.metadata.requires_dist or []
        extras = self.extras if self.extras else [""]

        for r in deps:
            if r.marker is None:
                yield r
            else:
                for e in extras:
                    if r.marker.evaluate({"extra": e}):
                        yield r

    @property
    def dependencies(self) -> list[Requirement]:
        if self._dependencies is None:
            dependencies = list(self._get_dependencies())
            object.__setattr__(self, "_dependencies", dependencies)
        assert self._dependencies
        return self._dependencies

    @property
    def requires_python(self) -> str | None:
        spec = self.metadata.requires_python
        return str(spec) if spec is not None else None


def get_metadata_for_wheel(
    url: str, metadata_url: str | None = None, *, validate: bool = True
) -> Metadata:
    """Get metadata for a wheel, supporting PEP 658 metadata endpoints.

    Read only the root dist-info directory matching the wheel filename.

    Args:
        url: URL of the wheel file
        metadata_url: Optional URL of the metadata file (PEP 658)
        validate: Whether to validate metadata (default: True)

    Returns:
        Parsed metadata as a Metadata object
    """
    # Try PEP 658 metadata endpoint first if available
    if metadata_url:
        try:
            logger.debug(
                f"Attempting to fetch metadata from PEP 658 endpoint: {metadata_url}"
            )
            response = session.get(metadata_url)
            response.raise_for_status()

            # Parse metadata directly using packaging.metadata.Metadata
            # (avoiding circular import with dependencies module)
            metadata = Metadata.from_email(response.content, validate=validate)
            logger.debug(f"Successfully retrieved metadata via PEP 658 for {url}")
            return metadata

        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug(f"Failed to fetch PEP 658 metadata from {metadata_url}: {e}")
            logger.debug(
                "Falling back to downloading full wheel for metadata extraction"
            )

    # Fallback to existing method: download wheel and extract metadata
    logger.debug(f"Downloading full wheel to extract metadata: {url}")
    data = session.get(url).content
    wheel_filename = unquote(urlparse(url).path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1])
    dist_name, dist_version, _ = wheel_filename.split("-", 2)
    metadata_path = f"{dist_name}-{dist_version}.dist-info/METADATA"
    with ZipFile(BytesIO(data)) as z:
        try:
            metadata_content = z.read(metadata_path)
        except KeyError as err:
            # If we didn't find the metadata, raise an error
            raise ValueError(f"Could not find METADATA file in wheel: {url}") from err
        # Parse metadata directly using packaging.metadata.Metadata
        # (avoiding circular import with dependencies module)
        return Metadata.from_email(metadata_content, validate=validate)

When AI agents create or significantly modify code, also add attribution:\n\n```text\ngit commit --signoff -m \"feat(scope): short summary\n\nBody explaining what and why.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #123\n```\n\nThis produces a commit message with both the `Signed-off-by` trailer (from `--signoff`) and the `Co-Authored-By` trailer.\n\n## Workflow for Complex Tasks\n\n1. **Search codebase** for similar patterns first\n2. **Create a checklist** for tracking progress\n3. **Work through items** one at a time\n4. **Run file-scoped tests** after each change\n5. **Run full quality checks** only at the end: `hatch run lint:fix && hatch run test:test && hatch run mypy:check && hatch run lint:check`\n\n---\n\n**See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for comprehensive standards, detailed examples, and design patterns.**\n# Contributing to Fromager\n\nFromager thrives on practical, well-tested contributions. This guide summarizes how to set up a workspace, follow our standards, and submit polished changes. Skim it once, keep it handy, and refer back whenever you are unsure.\n\n> **Note**: If you're using AI coding assistants, also see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for AI-optimized quick reference.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [Quick Start](#quick-start)\n- [Coding Standards](#coding-standards)\n- [Testing](#testing)\n- [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines)\n- [Before Submitting](#before-submitting)\n- [Design Patterns Used in Fromager](#design-patterns-used-in-fromager)\n- [Quick Reference](#quick-reference)\n- [Getting Help](#getting-help)\n- [Resources](#resources)\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.12 or newer\n\n- `hatch` for environment and task management\n\n  ```bash\n  pip install hatch\n  # or\n  pipx install hatch  # recommended\n  ```\n\n### Initial Setup\n\n```bash\n# 1. Fork the repository on GitHub\n# 2. Clone your fork\ngit clone https://github.com/<your-username>/fromager.git\ncd fromager\n\n# 3. Add upstream remote\ngit remote add upstream https://github.com/python-wheel-build/fromager.git\n\n# 4. Create development environment\nhatch env create\n\n# 5. Install pre-commit hooks (optional but recommended)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n```\n\n### Contribution Workflow\n\n```bash\n# 1. Sync with upstream\ngit checkout main\ngit fetch upstream\ngit merge upstream/main\n\n# 2. Create a feature branch\ngit checkout -b feat/<short-description>\n\n# 3. Make changes and test as you go\nhatch run test:test tests/test_<module>.py       # Test your specific changes\n\n# 4. Before committing, run full quality checks\nhatch run lint:precommit\n\n# 5. Commit using Conventional Commits\ngit commit -m \"feat(scope): short summary\"\n\n# 6. Push to your fork\ngit push origin feat/<short-description>\n\n# 7. Create a pull request on GitHub\n```\n\n### Pre-commit Hook (Recommended)\n\nTo ensure quality checks run automatically before each commit, install the pre-commit hooks that run linting, mypy type checking, and commit message validation:\n\n```bash\n# Install pre-commit hooks (run once after cloning)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n\n# The hooks automatically run linters before each commit and validate\n# that commit messages follow Conventional Commits format.\n\n# If a hook fails, it will prevent the commit and show helpful messages.\n# You can fix formatting issues automatically with:\nhatch run lint:fix\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hooks prevent commits that would fail CI quality checks, and enforce that all commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format documented in the [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines) section.\n\n---\n\n## Coding Standards\n\n### Type Annotations\n\n- Every function (including tests) must annotate all parameters and return values.\n- Use modern `X | None` syntax instead of `Optional[X]` (PEP 604).\n- Prefer precise collection types (`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, etc.).\n\n```python\ndef process(data: str | None, count: int = 0) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Process the input and return aggregate counts.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n```\n\n### Code Quality and Formatting\n\n- Ruff enforces both formatting and linting.\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to automatically format code.\n- See [Quick Reference](#quick-reference) for additional commands.\n\n### Import Organization\n\n- **PEP 8: imports should be at the top**: All import statements must be placed at the top of the file, after module docstrings and before other code.\n- **No local imports**: Do not place import statements inside functions, methods, or conditional blocks.\n\n### Documentation Expectations\n\n- Add a module docstring describing purpose and high-level behavior.\n- Public functions and classes require docstrings that cover arguments, return values, and noteworthy behavior.\n- Keep prose short and imperative; explain \"why\" decisions when the code itself cannot.\n\n```python\ndef retry_on_exception(\n    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...],\n    max_attempts: int = 5,\n) -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Retry decorated call on the provided exception types.\n\n    Args:\n        exceptions: Exception types that trigger a retry.\n        max_attempts: Maximum number of attempts.\n\n    Returns:\n        Decorator function.\n    \"\"\"\n    ...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never repeat the code literally.\n\n```python\n# Bad - comment just repeats the code\nx = x + 1  # increment x\n\n# Good - clear variable name makes the comment unnecessary\ntotal_attempts += 1\n\n# Good - comment explains the reasoning behind the approach\n# Exponential backoff avoids thundering herd when many jobs retry at once.\nwait_time = min(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1), max_backoff)\n```\n\n### Logging\n\n- Use a module-level logger and the appropriate log level for the situation.\n- When processing per-requirement work, wrap nested calls in `req_ctxvar_context()` so log records automatically include the package (and optional version). This keeps CLI logs searchable even when work runs in parallel.\n\n```python\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\ndef sync_artifacts() -> None:\n    logger.info(\"Starting artifact sync\")\n    logger.debug(\"Artifacts queued: %s\", pending_jobs)\n\n# When processing a specific package, wrap calls to include package info in logs\n# req: Requirement object for the package being processed\n# version: Version string being built (optional)\nwith req_ctxvar_context(req, version):\n    logger.info(\"Resolving build dependencies\")  # Logs will include package name\n```\n\n### Error Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = load_config(config_file)\n    # Assert\n    assert result[\"setting\"] == \"value\"\n```\n\n### Useful Commands\n\n```bash\nhatch run test:test                              # Full suite\nhatch run test:test tests/test_context.py        # Specific file\nhatch run test:test --log-level DEBUG            # Verbose output\nhatch run test:coverage-report                   # Coverage summary\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commit Guidelines\n\nFromager follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/).\n\n```text\n<type>(<scope>): <short summary>\n\n<body explaining what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        return value.strip()\n    raise TypeError(f\"unsupported type {type(value)}: {value!r}\")\n\nEnvKey = typing.Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_validate_envkey)]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n| -- | -- |\n| Run tests | `hatch run test:test` |\n| Check code quality | `hatch run lint:check` |\n| Fix formatting | `hatch run lint:fix` |\n| Type checking | `hatch run mypy:check` |\n\n### Standards\n\n| Standard | Requirement |\n| -- | -- |\n| Type annotations | Required for every function |\n| Docstrings | Required on public APIs |\n| Tests | Required for new behavior |\n| Trailing whitespace | Forbidden |\n| File endings | Single newline |\n| Commit format | Conventional Commits |\n\n---\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for discussion or questions or design proposals.\n- File an issue with a minimal reproduction for bugs.\n- Ask for targeted feedback type: ignore\nfrom packaging.requirements import Requirement\nfrom packaging.tags import Tag\nfrom packaging.utils import (\n    BuildTag,\n    canonicalize_name,\n    parse_wheel_filename,\n)\nfrom packaging.version import Version\n\nfrom . import (\n    dependencies,\n    external_commands,\n    metrics,\n    overrides,\n    packagesettings,\n    requirements_file,\n    resolver,\n    sbom,\n    sources,\n)\n\nif typing.TYPE_CHECKING:\n    from . import build_environment, context\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nFROMAGER_BUILD_SETTINGS = \"fromager-build-settings\"\nFROMAGER_ELF_PROVIDES = \"fromager-elf-provides.txt\"\nFROMAGER_ELF_REQUIRES = \"fromager-elf-requires.txt\"\nFROMAGER_BUILD_REQ_PREFIX = \"fromager\"\n\n\ndef _log_existing_sboms(\n    req: Requirement,\n    dist_info_dir: pathlib.Path,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Log any existing SBOM files found in the wheel's .dist-info/sboms/ directory.\"\"\"\n    sboms_dir = dist_info_dir / \"sboms\"\n    if not sboms_dir.is_dir():\n        return\n    sbom_files = sorted(sboms_dir.iterdir())\n    if sbom_files:\n        names = [f.name for f in sbom_files]\n        logger.info(\n            \"%s: found existing SBOM files in wheel: %s\",\n            req.name,\n            \", \".join(names),\n        )\n\n\ndef _extra_metadata_elfdeps(\n    ctx: context.WorkContext,\n    req: Requirement,\n    wheel_root_dir: pathlib.Path,\n    dist_info_dir: pathlib.Path,\n) -> typing.Iterable[elfdeps.ELFInfo]:\n    \"\"\"Analyze a wheel's ELF dependencies and add info files\n\n    Logs and returns library dependencies and library provides. Writes\n    requirements to dist-info.\n    \"\"\"\n    # mapping of required libraries to list of versions\n    requires: set[elfdeps.SOInfo] = set()\n    provides: set[elfdeps.SOInfo] = set()\n    runpaths: set[str] = set()\n    elfinfos: list[elfdeps.ELFInfo] = []\n\n    settings = elfdeps.ELFAnalyzeSettings(filter_soname=True)\n    for info in elfdeps.analyze_dirtree(wheel_root_dir, settings=settings):\n        if info.filename is not None:\n            relname = str(info.filename.relative_to(wheel_root_dir))\n        else:\n            relname = \"n/a\"\n        logger.debug(\n            f\"{relname} ({info.soname}) \"\n            f\"requires {sorted(info.requires)}, \"\n            f\"provides {sorted(info.provides)}\"\n        )\n        provides.update(info.provides)\n        requires.update(info.requires)\n        if info.runpath is not None:\n            runpaths.update(info.runpath)\n        elfinfos.append(info)\n\n    # Don't list provided names as requirements\n    requires = requires.difference(provides)\n\n    if requires:\n        reqmap: dict[str, list[str]] = collections.defaultdict(list)\n        for r in requires:\n            reqmap[r.soname].append(r.version)\n\n        names = sorted(\n            name for name in reqmap if not name.startswith((\"ld-linux\", \"rtld\"))\n        )\n        logger.info(\"Requires libraries: %s\", \", \".join(names))\n        for name, versions in sorted(reqmap.items()):\n            logger.debug(\n                \"Requires %s(%s)\",\n                name,\n                \", \".join(v for v in versions if v),\n            )\n\n        requires_file = dist_info_dir / FROMAGER_ELF_REQUIRES\n        with requires_file.open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n            for soinfo in sorted(requires):\n                f.write(f\"{soinfo}\\n\")\n\n    if provides:\n        names = sorted(p.soname for p in provides)\n        logger.info(\"Provides libraries: %s\", \", \".join(names))\n\n        provides_file = dist_info_dir / FROMAGER_ELF_PROVIDES\n        with provides_file.open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n            for soinfo in sorted(provides):\n                f.write(f\"{soinfo}\\n\")\n\n    if runpaths:\n        logger.info(\"Libraries have runpath: %s\", \" \".join(sorted(runpaths)))\n\n    return elfinfos\n\n\ndef extract_info_from_wheel_file(\n    req: Requirement, wheel_file: pathlib.Path\n) -> tuple[str, Version, BuildTag, frozenset[Tag]]:\n    \"\"\"Extract metadata from a wheel filename.\n\n    Returns the **verbatim** dist name (not normalized) because the\n    dist-info directory inside the wheel uses the original casing\n    (e.g. ``MarkupSafe``, not ``markupsafe``). Uses ``parse_wheel_filename``\n    for validation and to extract version, build tag, and platform tags.\n    \"\"\"\n    # parse_wheel_filename normalizes the dist name, however the dist-info\n    # directory uses the verbatim distribution name from the wheel file.\n    # Packages with upper case names like \"MarkupSafe\" are affected.\n    dist_name_normalized, dist_version, build_tag, wheel_tags = parse_wheel_filename(\n        wheel_file.name\n    )\n    dist_name = wheel_file.name.split(\"-\", 1)[0]\n    if dist_name_normalized != canonicalize_name(dist_name):\n        # sanity check, should never fail\n        raise ValueError(f\"{dist_name_normalized} does not match {dist_name}\")\n    return (dist_name, dist_version, build_tag, wheel_tags)\n\n\ndef default_add_extra_metadata_to_wheels(\n    ctx: context.WorkContext,\n    req: Requirement,\n    version: Version,\n    extra_environ: dict[str, str],\n    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path,\n    dist_info_dir: pathlib.Path,\n) -> dict[str, typing.Any]:\n    \"\"\"Default implementation returns empty dict - no extra metadata.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n\n\n@metrics.timeit(description=\"add extra metadata to wheels\")\ndef add_extra_metadata_to_wheels(\n    *,\n    ctx: context.WorkContext,\n    req: Requirement,\n    version: Version,\n    extra_environ: dict[str, str],\n    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path,\n    wheel_file: pathlib.Path,\n) -> pathlib.Path:\n    \"\"\"Unpack a wheel, inject extra metadata, and repack with a build tag.\n\n    Unpacks the wheel, validates dist-info, adds plugin metadata, build\n    settings, requirement files, ELF dependency info (Linux only), and\n    an SBOM. Repacks with ``wheel pack`` and deletes the original.\n    \"\"\"\n    pbi = ctx.package_build_info(req)\n    dist_name, dist_version, _, wheel_tags = extract_info_from_wheel_file(\n        req, wheel_file\n    )\n    dist_filename = f\"{dist_name}-{dist_version}\"\n\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as dir_name:\n        wheel_root_dir = pathlib.Path(dir_name) / dist_filename\n        wheel_root_dir.mkdir()\n        with zipfile.ZipFile(str(wheel_file)) as zf:\n            for infolist in zf.filelist:\n                # Check for path traversal attempts\n                if (\n                    os.path.isabs(infolist.filename)\n                    or \"..\" in pathlib.Path(infolist.filename).parts\n                ):\n                    raise ValueError(f\"Unsafe path in wheel: {infolist.filename}\")\n                zf.extract(infolist, wheel_root_dir)\n                # the higher 16 bits store the permissions and type of file (i.e. stat.filemode)\n                # the lower bits of this give us the permission\n                permissions = infolist.external_attr >> 16 & 0o777\n                wheel_root_dir.joinpath(infolist.filename).chmod(permissions)\n\n        dist_info_dir = wheel_root_dir / f\"{dist_filename}.dist-info\"\n        if not dist_info_dir.is_dir():\n            raise ValueError(f\"{wheel_file} does not contain {dist_info_dir.name}\")\n\n        _log_existing_sboms(req, dist_info_dir)\n\n        data_to_add = overrides.find_and_invoke(\n            req.name,\n            \"add_extra_metadata_to_wheels\",\n            default_add_extra_metadata_to_wheels,\n            ctx=ctx,\n            req=req,\n            version=version,\n            extra_environ=extra_environ,\n            sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,\n            dist_info_dir=dist_info_dir,\n        )\n        if not isinstance(data_to_add, dict):\n            logger.warning(\n                \"unexpected return type from plugin add_extra_metadata_to_wheels. Expected dictionary. Will ignore\"\n            )\n            data_to_add = {}\n\n        if pbi.has_config:\n            settings = pbi.serialize(mode=\"json\", exclude_defaults=False)\n        else:\n            settings = {}\n        if data_to_add:\n            settings[\"metadata-from-plugin\"] = data_to_add\n        build_file = dist_info_dir / FROMAGER_BUILD_SETTINGS\n        build_file.write_text(tomlkit.dumps(settings))\n\n        req_files = sdist_root_dir.parent.glob(\"*-requirements.txt\")\n        for req_file in req_files:\n            shutil.copy(\n                req_file, dist_info_dir / f\"{FROMAGER_BUILD_REQ_PREFIX}-{req_file.name}\"\n            )\n\n        if any(tag.platform != \"all\" for tag in wheel_tags):\n            # platlib wheel\n            if sys.platform == \"linux\":\n                _extra_metadata_elfdeps(\n                    ctx=ctx,\n                    req=req,\n                    wheel_root_dir=wheel_root_dir,\n                    dist_info_dir=dist_info_dir,\n                )\n            else:\n                logger.debug(\n                    \"shared library dependency analysis not implemented for %s\",\n                    sys.platform,\n                )\n        else:\n            logger.debug(\"%s is a purelib wheel\", req.name)\n\n        sbom_settings = ctx.settings.sbom_settings\n        if sbom_settings is not None:\n            sbom_doc = sbom.generate_sbom(\n                ctx=ctx,\n                req=req,\n                version=version,\n            )\n            sbom.write_sbom(sbom=sbom_doc, dist_info_dir=dist_info_dir)\n\n        build_tag_from_settings = pbi.build_tag(version)\n        build_tag = build_tag_from_settings if build_tag_from_settings else (0, \"\")\n\n        cmd = Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n---\nname: surgical-patch\ndescription: Fix bugs and small behavior changes at the narrowest responsible layer. Use when regression proof, preserved surrounding behavior, and task-relevant tests matter.\n---\n\n# Surgical patch\n\nReproduce failure first when economical; otherwise capture strongest available evidence.\n\n- Trace symptom to responsible mechanism.\n- Change narrowest layer that owns incorrect behavior.\n- Preserve unrelated behavior and user changes.\n- Avoid cleanup, renaming, and abstraction outside fix.\n- Add only regression proof relevant to task.\n\nRun focused proof plus nearest affected gate. Stop when failure is fixed and regression proof passes.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
