"""Tests for PEP 658 metadata support."""

import typing
from io import BytesIO
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
from zipfile import ZipFile

import pytest
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager.candidate import Candidate, get_metadata_for_wheel


class TestPEP658Support:
    """Test PEP 658 metadata support in fromager."""

    def test_candidate_with_metadata_url(self) -> None:
        """Test that Candidate can be created with a metadata URL."""
        candidate = Candidate(
            name="test-package",
            version=Version("1.0.0"),
            url="https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            has_metadata=True,
        )

        assert (
            candidate.metadata_url
            == "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata"
        )

    def test_candidate_without_metadata_url(self) -> None:
        """Test that Candidate works without metadata URL (legacy behavior)."""
        candidate = Candidate(
            name="test-package",
            version=Version("1.0.0"),
            url="https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
        )

        assert candidate.metadata_url is None

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_with_pep658_success(self, mock_session: typing.Any) -> None:
        """Test successful metadata retrieval via PEP 658 endpoint."""
        # Mock the metadata response
        mock_response = Mock()
        mock_response.content = b"""Metadata-Version: 2.1
Name: test-package
Version: 1.0.0
Summary: A test package
Requires-Dist: requests >= 2.0.0
"""
        mock_response.raise_for_status.return_value = None
        mock_session.get.return_value = mock_response

        wheel_url = "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"
        metadata_url = (
            "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata"
        )

        metadata = get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url)

        # Verify the metadata was parsed correctly
        assert metadata.name == "test-package"
        assert str(metadata.version) == "1.0.0"
        assert metadata.summary == "A test package"
        assert metadata.requires_dist is not None
        assert any(str(req) == "requests>=2.0.0" for req in metadata.requires_dist)

        # Verify only the metadata URL was called, not the wheel URL
        mock_session.get.assert_called_once_with(metadata_url)

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_pep658_fallback_behavior(
        self, mock_session: typing.Any
    ) -> None:
        """Test that PEP 658 is tried first, then falls back to wheel download."""
        # Mock that metadata URL fails, then wheel URL succeeds
        responses = []

        def side_effect(url: str) -> typing.Any:
            if url.endswith(".metadata"):
                # First call - metadata request fails
                mock_response = Mock()
                mock_response.raise_for_status.side_effect = Exception("404 Not Found")
                responses.append(("metadata", url))
                return mock_response
            else:
                # Second call - wheel request
                responses.append(("wheel", url))
                raise Exception("Wheel parsing intentionally mocked to fail")

        mock_session.get.side_effect = side_effect

        wheel_url = "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"
        metadata_url = (
            "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata"
        )

        # This should raise an exception during wheel parsing, but we can verify the order
        try:
            get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url)
        except Exception:
            pass  # Expected to fail during wheel parsing mock

        # Verify that both URLs were called in the correct order
        assert len(responses) == 2
        assert responses[0] == ("metadata", metadata_url)
        assert responses[1] == ("wheel", wheel_url)
        assert mock_session.get.call_count == 2

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        ("dist_name", "dist_version", "wheel_url"),
        [
            (
                "test_package",
                "1.0.0",
                "https://pkg.test/test_package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            ),
            (
                "MarkupSafe",
                "3.0.0",
                "https://pkg.test/MarkupSafe-3.0.0-1-py3-none-any.whl",
            ),
            (
                "test_package",
                "1.0+local",
                "https://pkg.test/test_package-1.0%2Blocal-py3-none-any.whl?download=1#sha256=abc",
            ),
        ],
    )
    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_ignores_vendored_metadata(
        self,
        mock_session: Mock,
        dist_name: str,
        dist_version: str,
        wheel_url: str,
    ) -> None:
        """Read the wheel's root metadata even when other metadata appears first."""
        vendored_metadata = (
            "Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: vendored\nVersion: 9.9\n"
            "Requires-Dist: vendored-dependency\n"
        )
        wheel_data = BytesIO()
        with ZipFile(wheel_data, "w") as wheel:
            for metadata_path in (
                f"{dist_name}/_vendor/vendored-9.9.dist-info/METADATA",
                "vendored-9.9.dist-info/METADATA",
                f"{dist_name}-9.9.dist-info/METADATA",
                f"{dist_name}/_vendor/{dist_name}-{dist_version}.dist-info/METADATA",
            ):
                wheel.writestr(metadata_path, vendored_metadata)
            wheel.writestr(
                f"{dist_name}-{dist_version}.dist-info/METADATA",
                f"Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: {dist_name}\nVersion: {dist_version}\n"
                "Requires-Dist: wheel-dependency>=1.0\n",
            )
        mock_session.get.return_value.content = wheel_data.getvalue()

        metadata = get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url)

        assert metadata.name == dist_name
        assert metadata.version == Version(dist_version)
        assert metadata.requires_dist is not None
        assert [str(req) for req in metadata.requires_dist] == ["wheel-dependency>=1.0"]
        mock_session.get.assert_called_once_with(wheel_url)

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "metadata_path",
        [
            "test_package/_vendor/test_package-1.0.0.dist-info/METADATA",
            "vendored-9.9.dist-info/METADATA",
            "test_package-9.9.dist-info/METADATA",
        ],
    )
    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_rejects_missing_wheel_metadata(
        self, mock_session: Mock, metadata_path: str
    ) -> None:
        """Raise an error when only unrelated or nested metadata is present."""
        wheel_data = BytesIO()
        with ZipFile(wheel_data, "w") as wheel:
            wheel.writestr(
                metadata_path,
                "Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: vendored\nVersion: 9.9\n",
            )
        mock_session.get.return_value.content = wheel_data.getvalue()
        wheel_url = "https://pkg.test/test_package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"

        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Could not find METADATA file in wheel"):
            get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url)

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_without_pep658_behavior(
        self, mock_session: typing.Any
    ) -> None:
        """Test that without PEP 658 metadata URL, only wheel URL is called."""
        # Mock wheel request
        responses = []

Resolver Architecture
=====================

Fromager resolves package versions from multiple sources using a
provider abstraction.  This document describes the resolution
strategies, filtering, and key design decisions.

.. seealso::

   :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.
   :doc:`bootstrapper-architecture` covers how resolution fits into the
   bootstrap pipeline.

Resolution Strategies
---------------------

During bootstrap, the resolver coordinator tries these sources in
priority order and accumulates results in a thread-safe session cache:

.. code-block:: text

   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │               Resolution Priority Order               │
   │                                                       │
   │  1. Session cache (versions found earlier)            │
   │          │ miss                                       │
   │          ▼                                            │
   │  2. Previous dependency graph (prior run)             │
   │          │ miss                                       │
   │          ▼                                            │
   │  3. Network (PyPI / GitHub / GitLab)                  │
   │     (per-package configurable)                        │
   │          │ age filter empties result                  │
   │          ▼                                            │
   │  4. Cache server fallback                             │
   │     (multiple_versions mode only)                     │
   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

   Git URL requirements (top-level only) bypass this
   chain entirely: the repo is cloned and the version
   is extracted from package metadata.

Versions discovered from any source are merged into the session cache.
Subsequent requests for the same package skip the network entirely if
the cache already contains a matching version.

Provider Hierarchy
------------------

All resolution sources inherit from ``BaseProvider``, which implements
the resolvelib ``ExtrasProvider`` interface.  The bootstrap engine and
CLI commands interact with providers through a common
``find_matches()`` method.

.. code-block:: text

   BaseProvider
   ├── PyPIProvider         (PEP 503 Simple API)
   │   └── PyPICacheProvider  (fromager's own wheel server)
   ├── GenericProvider      (callback-based, parses tags)
   │   ├── GitHubTagProvider
   │   └── GitLabTagProvider
   └── VersionMapProvider   (pre-resolved version→URL map)

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 75

   * - Provider
     - What it queries
   * - ``PyPIProvider``
     - Any PEP 503 Simple API index (pypi.org, custom mirrors).
       Filters by platform tags, Python version, and yanked status.
   * - ``PyPICacheProvider``
     - Subclass of ``PyPIProvider`` pointing at fromager's own wheel
       server.  No cooldown applied.  Used as a fallback when age
       filtering eliminates all candidates.
   * - ``GenericProvider``
     - Callback-based provider that pairs a version source function
       with a configurable match function (plain parse or regex).
       Base class for the tag providers below.
   * - ``GitHubTagProvider``
     - GitHub REST API for repository tags.  Versions are parsed
       from tag names using a configurable pattern.
   * - ``GitLabTagProvider``
     - GitLab REST API for repository tags.  Includes upload
       timestamps for age filtering.
   * - ``VersionMapProvider``
     - Wraps a pre-built ``VersionMap`` (version → URL mapping).
       Used when versions are already known, e.g. from a prior
       resolution or a settings-provided URL template.

Per-package settings in YAML can select which provider to use and
configure its parameters (index URL, tag pattern, etc.).  Override
plugins can replace the provider entirely for a specific package via
the ``get_resolver_provider`` hook.

Version Filtering Window
-------------------------

Two age-based filters can narrow the set of acceptable versions:

.. code-block:: text

   ◄── too old ──┤  acceptable window  ├── too new ──►

                 │                      │
            max_age cutoff         cooldown cutoff
          (reject before this)   (reject after this)

- **Cooldown** rejects releases that are too new.  It ensures a
  minimum time has passed since publication, guarding against
  problematic releases.  Configurable per package; bypassed for
  exact version pins (``==``).

- **Max age** rejects releases that are too old.  Used primarily in
  ``multiple_versions`` mode to limit the range of versions built.
  Packages with a constraint in the provider's constraints skip this
  filter to honor explicit user intent.

.. versionchanged:: next
   Constrained packages bypass max-age filtering in both modes.

When both are active, only versions published within the window are
considered for unconstrained packages.  If all candidates are filtered
out, the behavior depends on the mode: in single-version mode a warning
is logged and all candidates are kept; in ``multiple_versions`` mode
the cache server fallback is tried instead.

Flat Resolution by Design
-------------------------

Fromager deliberately does **not** use resolvelib's transitive
dependency resolution.  Every provider's ``get_dependencies()`` method
returns an empty list.  This means resolution is a simple "find the
best matching version" operation, not a full constraint solver with
backtracking.

Transitive dependencies are handled by the bootstrap engine's own DFS
loop: after a package is built, its install dependencies are extracted
from the wheel metadata and pushed onto the work stack as new
``RESOLVE`` phase items.  This separation keeps the resolver stateless
and makes each resolution call independent and thread-safe.

Per-Package Configuration
-------------------------

Package settings files (YAML) can configure the resolver for each
package independently: resolver type (PyPI, GitHub tags, GitLab tags,
hook-based, or blocked), index URL, cooldown, tag pattern, and
override plugins.

See :doc:`package-settings` for how settings are loaded and merged.

@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=200)
def match_py_req(py_req: str, *, python_version: Version = PYTHON_VERSION) -> bool:
    """Python version requirement lookup with LRU cache

    Raises InvalidSpecifier on error

    SpecifierSet parsing and matching takes a non-trivial amount of time. A
    bootstrap run can spend over 10% of its time in parsing and matching
    Python version requirements.

    This function caches the result of SpecifierSet parsing and contains
    operation for Python version requirement. Most packages share similar
    constraints, e.g. ``>= 3.10``.
    """
    return python_version in SpecifierSet(py_req)


def resolve(
    *,
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool = True,
    include_wheels: bool = True,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> tuple[str, Version]:
    """Resolve requirement and return the best matching version.

    Returns (url, version) tuple for the highest matching version.
    """
    # Create the (reusable) resolver.
    provider = overrides.find_and_invoke(
        req.name,
        "get_resolver_provider",
        default_resolver_provider,
        ctx=ctx,
        req=req,
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )
    provider.cooldown = resolve_package_cooldown(ctx, req, req_type=req_type)
    max_age_cutoff = _compute_max_age_cutoff(ctx)
    results = find_all_matching_from_provider(
        provider, req, max_age_cutoff=max_age_cutoff
    )
    return results[0]


def default_resolver_provider(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool,
    include_wheels: bool,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> (
    PyPIProvider
    | GenericProvider
    | GitHubTagProvider
    | GitLabTagProvider
    | VersionMapProvider
):
    """Lookup resolver provider to resolve package versions"""
    return PyPIProvider(
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        constraints=ctx.constraints,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )


def _has_equality_pin(req: Requirement) -> bool:
    """Return True if the requirement has a single exact ``==`` pin.

    Rejects wildcard pins (``==1.*``) and compound specifiers (``==1,>2``)
    which are not true exact version pins.
    """
    specs = list(req.specifier)
    return len(specs) == 1 and specs[0].operator == "==" and "*" not in specs[0].version


def resolve_package_cooldown(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
) -> Cooldown | None:
    """Compute the effective cooldown for a single package.

    Args:
        ctx: The current work context (provides the global cooldown).
        req: The package requirement being resolved.
        req_type: The requirement type (top-level, install, etc.).

    Returns:
        The cooldown to pass to the provider, or ``None`` if disabled.
    """
    if req_type == RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL and _has_equality_pin(req):
        if ctx.cooldown is not None:
            logger.info("cooldown bypassed as the top-level requirement uses == pin")
        return None

    per_package_days = ctx.package_build_info(req).resolver_min_release_age
    global_cooldown = ctx.cooldown
    if per_package_days is None:
        return global_cooldown
    if per_package_days == 0:
        return None
    # Per-package positive override: inherit bootstrap_time from global so all
    # resolutions in a single run share the same fixed cutoff point.
    bootstrap_time = (
        global_cooldown.bootstrap_time
        if global_cooldown is not None
        else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
    )
    return Cooldown(
        min_age=datetime.timedelta(days=per_package_days),
        bootstrap_time=bootstrap_time,
    )

See `tests/test_context.py` for examples.\n\n## Documentation and doc strings\n\n- Use single backticks around function and class names in markdown (e.g. `req_ctxvar_context()`, `WorkContext`), double backticks in .rst (reStructuredText)\n- Use Sphinx `versionadded`, `versionremoved`, `versionchanged` directives for user-facing changes (get next version from last git tag)\n- When code changes affect the architecture described in `docs/concepts/`, update the relevant doc:\n  - `architecture-overview.rst` — major subsystems, data flow, extension points, key data structures\n  - `bootstrapper-architecture.rst` — phase pipeline, class hierarchy, bootstrapper-phase interaction\n  - `resolver-architecture.rst` — resolution strategies, provider hierarchy, version filtering\n  - `hooks-and-overrides.rst` — override hook points, global hooks, plugin discovery\n  - `package-settings.rst` — settings loading flow, merge order, PackageBuildInfo facade\n\n## Commit Messages\n\nFollow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for format, types, and examples.\n\nUse backticks around function and class names (e.g. `WorkContext`)\n\nAlways use `--signoff` to add a DCO sign-off. When AI agents create or significantly modify code, also add attribution:\n\n```text\ngit commit --signoff -m \"feat(scope): short summary\n\nBody explaining what and why.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #123\n```\n\nThis produces a commit message with both the `Signed-off-by` trailer (from `--signoff`) and the `Co-Authored-By` trailer.\n\n## End-to-end tests\n\nThere is a set of end-to-end tests in `./e2e`. Files named like\n`test_*.sh` are test scripts and files named like `ci_*.sh` are CI\ntest suites that run the individual test scripts.\n\nThe end-to-end tests are expensive so **ONLY** run them when asked.\n\nThe CI test suites produce a lot of output. The most important\ninformation is in the summary at the end, where it shows which test\nscripts fail. Always run CI jobs in a way that only adds the last 25\nlines to the context window, then run an individual failing test\nscript to debug the problem.\n\n## Workflow for Complex Tasks\n\n1. **Search codebase** for similar patterns first\n2. **Create a checklist** for tracking progress\n3. **Work through items** one at a time\n4. **Run file-scoped tests** after each change\n5. **Run full quality checks** only at the end: `hatch run lint:fix && hatch run test:test && hatch run mypy:check && hatch run lint:check`\n\n---\n\n**See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for comprehensive standards, detailed examples, and design patterns.**\n# Contributing to Fromager\n\nFromager thrives on practical, well-tested contributions. This guide summarizes how to set up a workspace, follow our standards, and submit polished changes. Skim it once, keep it handy, and refer back whenever you are unsure.\n\n> **Note**: If you're using AI coding assistants, also see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for AI-optimized quick reference.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [Quick Start](#quick-start)\n- [Coding Standards](#coding-standards)\n- [Testing](#testing)\n- [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines)\n- [Before Submitting](#before-submitting)\n- [Design Patterns Used in Fromager](#design-patterns-used-in-fromager)\n- [Quick Reference](#quick-reference)\n- [Getting Help](#getting-help)\n- [Resources](#resources)\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.12 or newer\n\n- `hatch` for environment and task management\n\n  ```bash\n  pip install hatch\n  # or\n  pipx install hatch  # recommended\n  ```\n\n### Initial Setup\n\n```bash\n# 1. Fork the repository on GitHub\n# 2. Clone your fork\ngit clone https://github.com/<your-username>/fromager.git\ncd fromager\n\n# 3. Add upstream remote\ngit remote add upstream https://github.com/python-wheel-build/fromager.git\n\n# 4. Create development environment\nhatch env create\n\n# 5. Install pre-commit hooks (optional but recommended)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n```\n\n### Contribution Workflow\n\n```bash\n# 1. Sync with upstream\ngit checkout main\ngit fetch upstream\ngit merge upstream/main\n\n# 2. Create a feature branch\ngit checkout -b feat/<short-description>\n\n# 3. Make changes and test as you go\nhatch run test:test tests/test_<module>.py       # Test your specific changes\n\n# 4. Before committing, run full quality checks\nhatch run lint:precommit\n\n# 5. Commit using Conventional Commits\ngit commit -m \"feat(scope): short summary\"\n\n# 6. Push to your fork\ngit push origin feat/<short-description>\n\n# 7. Create a pull request on GitHub\n```\n\n### Pre-commit Hook (Recommended)\n\nTo ensure quality checks run automatically before each commit, install the pre-commit hooks that run linting, mypy type checking, and commit message validation:\n\n```bash\n# Install pre-commit hooks (run once after cloning)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n\n# The hooks automatically run linters before each commit and validate\n# that commit messages follow Conventional Commits format.\n\n# If a hook fails, it will prevent the commit and show helpful messages.\n# You can fix formatting issues automatically with:\nhatch run lint:fix\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hooks prevent commits that would fail CI quality checks, and enforce that all commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format documented in the [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines) section.\n\n---\n\n## Coding Standards\n\n### Type Annotations\n\n- Every function (including tests) must annotate all parameters and return values.\n- Use modern `X | None` syntax instead of `Optional[X]` (PEP 604).\n- Prefer precise collection types (`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, etc.).\n\n```python\ndef process(data: str | None, count: int = 0) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Process the input and return aggregate counts.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n```\n\n### Code Quality and Formatting\n\n- Ruff enforces both formatting and linting.\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to automatically format code.\n- See [Quick Reference](#quick-reference) for additional commands.\n\n### Import Organization\n\n- **PEP 8: imports should be at the top**: All import statements must be placed at the top of the file, after module docstrings and before other code.\n- **No local imports**: Do not place import statements inside functions, methods, or conditional blocks.\n\n### Documentation Expectations\n\n- Add a module docstring describing purpose and high-level behavior.\n- Public functions and classes require docstrings that cover arguments, return values, and noteworthy behavior.\n- Keep prose short and imperative; explain \"why\" decisions when the code itself cannot.\n\n```python\ndef retry_on_exception(\n    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...],\n    max_attempts: int = 5,\n) -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Retry decorated call on the provided exception types.\n\n    Args:\n        exceptions: Exception types that trigger a retry.\n        max_attempts: Maximum number of attempts.\n\n    Returns:\n        Decorator function.\n    \"\"\"\n    ...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never repeat the code literally.\n\n```python\n# Bad - comment just repeats the code\nx = x + 1  # increment x\n\n# Good - clear variable name makes the comment unnecessary\ntotal_attempts += 1\n\n# Good - comment explains the reasoning behind the approach\n# Exponential backoff avoids thundering herd when many jobs retry at once.\nwait_time = min(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1), max_backoff)\n```\n\n### Logging\n\n- Use a module-level logger and the appropriate log level for the situation.\n- When processing per-requirement work, wrap nested calls in `req_ctxvar_context()` so log records automatically include the package (and optional version). This keeps CLI logs searchable even when work runs in parallel.\n\n```python\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\ndef sync_artifacts() -> None:\n    logger.info(\"Starting artifact sync\")\n    logger.debug(\"Artifacts queued: %s\", pending_jobs)\n\n# When processing a specific package, wrap calls to include package info in logs\n# req: Requirement object for the package being processed\n# version: Version string being built (optional)\nwith req_ctxvar_context(req, version):\n    logger.info(\"Resolving build dependencies\")  # Logs will include package name\n```\n\n### Error Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = load_config(config_file)\n    # Assert\n    assert result[\"setting\"] == \"value\"\n```\n\n### Useful Commands\n\n```bash\nhatch run test:test                              # Full suite\nhatch run test:test tests/test_context.py        # Specific file\nhatch run test:test --log-level DEBUG            # Verbose output\nhatch run test:coverage-report                   # Coverage summary\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commit Guidelines\n\nFromager follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/).\n\n```text\n<type>(<scope>): <short summary>\n\n<body explaining what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        return value.strip()\n    raise TypeError(f\"unsupported type {type(value)}: {value!r}\")\n\nEnvKey = typing.Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_validate_envkey)]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n| -- | -- |\n| Run tests | `hatch run test:test` |\n| Check code quality | `hatch run lint:check` |\n| Fix formatting | `hatch run lint:fix` |\n| Type checking | `hatch run mypy:check` |\n\n### Standards\n\n| Standard | Requirement |\n| -- | -- |\n| Type annotations | Required for every function |\n| Docstrings | Required on public APIs |\n| Tests | Required for new behavior |\n| Trailing whitespace | Forbidden |\n| File endings | Single newline |\n| Commit format | Conventional Commits |\n\n---\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for discussion or questions or design proposals.\n- File an issue with a minimal reproduction for bugs.\n- Ask for targeted feedback directly in your pull request.\n\n## Resources\n\n- [PEP 8 - Style Guide](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008/)\n- [PEP 484 - Type Hints](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0484/)\n- [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)\n- [pytest Documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [Ruff Documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)\n\n---\n\n**Thanks for contributing to Fromager!** If you spot gaps or have suggestions for this guide, open an issue or start a discussion—we love improving our contributor experience.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_5","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc 'cat /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/caveman/SKILL.md /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/surgical-patch/SKILL.md'","aggregated_output":"---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n---\nname: surgical-patch\ndescription: Fix bugs and small behavior changes at the narrowest responsible layer. Use when regression proof, preserved surrounding behavior, and task-relevant tests matter.\n---\n\n# Surgical patch\n\nReproduce failure first when economical; otherwise capture strongest available evidence.\n\n- Trace symptom to responsible mechanism.\n- Change narrowest layer that owns incorrect behavior.\n- Preserve unrelated behavior and user changes.\n- Avoid cleanup, renaming, and abstraction outside fix.\n- Add only regression proof relevant to task.\n\nRun focused proof plus nearest affected gate. Stop when failure is fixed and regression proof passes.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

'1,150p' tests/test_context.py\"","aggregated_output":"\"\"\"Tests for the release-age cooldown policy (issue #877).\n\nThe cooldown rejects package versions published fewer than N days     if not blocked:\n                logger.debug(\"combining constraints %s and %s\", previous, req)\n                new_specifier = req.specifier & previous.specifier\n                if new_specifier.is_unsatisfiable():\n                    raise InvalidConstraintError(\n                        f\"Combined specifier '{new_specifier}' is not satisfiable \"\n                        f\"(existing: {previous}, new: {req})\"\n                    )\n                req.specifier = new_specifier\n        else:\n            logger.debug(f\"adding constraint {req}\")\n\n        self._data[canon_name] = req\n\n    def load_constraints_file(self, constraints_file: str | pathlib.Path) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Load constraints from a constraints file or URL\"\"\"\n        logger.info(\"loading constraints from %s\", constraints_file)\n        content = requirements_file.parse_requirements_file(constraints_file)\n        for line in content:\n            self.add_constraint(line)\n\n    def dump_constraints(self, output: typing.TextIO) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Dump combined constraints to a text stream\"\"\"\n        # sort by normalized name\n        for _, req in sorted(self._data.items()):\n            # write requirement without markers. They have been evaluated\n            # in add_constraint()\n            output.write(f\"{req.name}{req.specifier}\\n\")\n\n    def get_constraint(self, name: str) -> Requirement | None:\n        return self._data.get(canonicalize_name(name))\n\n    def allow_prerelease(self, pkg_name: str) -> bool:\n        constraint = self.get_constraint(pkg_name)\n        if constraint:\n            return bool(constraint.specifier.prereleases)\n        return False\n\n    def is_blocked(self, pkg_name: str) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Return True if the package is blocked by a ``<0`` constraint.\"\"\"\n        constraint = self.get_constraint(pkg_name)\n        if constraint:\n            return _is_blocked_specifier(constraint.specifier)\n        return False\n\n    def is_satisfied_by(self, pkg_name: str, version: Version) -> bool:\n        constraint = self.get_constraint(pkg_name)\n        if constraint:\n            return constraint.specifier.contains(version, prereleases=True)\n        return True\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

They are useful when you want to specify a version\nof a package other than the default (usually the latest version).\n\nBecause several commands in fromager use constraints, you pass them to the base\ncommand using the ``--constraints-file`` option.\n\nFor example, if you want to bootstrap a package that requires ``setuptools``\nand you want to avoid a breaking change in ``setuptools`` you can create a\nconstraints file that tells fromager to avoid using the latest version of\n``setuptools``:\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   setuptools<80.0.0\n\nThen you would run the following command:\n\n.. code-block:: console\n\n   $ fromager --constraints-file constraints.txt bootstrap my-package\n\nThis will use the constraints in the ``constraints.txt`` file to build\n``my-package``.\n\nUse the same constraints file with ``fromager build-sequence`` when building the\nproduction packages.\n\n.. code-block:: console\n\n   $ fromager --constraints-file constraints.txt build-sequence ./work-dir/build-order.json\n\nThis will use the constraints in the ``constraints.txt`` file to build the\nproduction packages for ``my-package``.\n\nMultiple constraints and remote constraints\n-------------------------------------------\n\n.. versionchanged:: 0.84.0\n   The ``--constraints-file`` / ``-c`` option now supports an arbitrary\n   number of arguments.\n\nThe ``--constraints-file`` argument can be supplied multiple times. Multiple\noccurrences of the same package are merged and validated. For example\n``egg>=1.0`` and ``egg!=1.1.2`` are combined into ``egg>=1.0,!=1.1.2``. An\nunsatisfiable combination like ``egg<1.0`` and ``egg>2.0`` is an error.\n\nFromager can load constraints from `https://` URLs, too.\n\n.. code-block:: console\n\n   $ fromager -c constraints.txt -c local-constraints.txt -c https://company.example/security-constraints.txt bootstrap my-package\n\nBlocking packages\n-----------------\n\nTo block a package entirely so that no version is accepted, use the special\nconstraint ``<0`` (or equivalently ``<0.0`` or ``<0.0.0``). No valid Python\nversion can satisfy this specifier, so the package is effectively excluded from\nthe build.\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   unwanted-package<0\n\nA blocked constraint cannot be combined with a regular constraint for the same\npackage. """Tests for the release-age cooldown policy (issue #877).

The cooldown rejects package versions published fewer than N days ago,
protecting against supply-chain attacks where a malicious version is
published and immediately pulled in by automated builds.
"""

import datetime
import logging
import pathlib
import re
import typing

import pytest
import requests_mock
import resolvelib
import yaml

from packaging.version import Version

    candidate,
    constraints,
    context,
    packagesettings,
    resolver,
    sources,
    wheels,
)
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

_BOOTSTRAP_TIME = datetime.datetime(2026, 3, 26, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS = datetime.timedelta(days=7)
# cutoff = 2026-03-19T00:00:00Z

# Use PEP 691 JSON format — pypi_simple reliably parses upload-time from JSON.
_PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json"

#   2.0.0  uploaded 2026-03-24 →  2 days old (within cooldown)
#   1.3.2  uploaded 2026-03-15 → 11 days old (outside cooldown)
#   1.2.2  uploaded 2026-01-01 → 84 days old (outside cooldown)

    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:

Resolver Architecture
=====================

Fromager resolves package versions from multiple sources using a
provider abstraction.  This document describes the resolution
strategies, filtering, and key design decisions.

.. seealso::

   :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.
   :doc:`bootstrapper-architecture` covers how resolution fits into the
   bootstrap pipeline.

Resolution Strategies
---------------------

During bootstrap, the resolver coordinator tries these sources in
priority order and accumulates results in a thread-safe session cache:

.. code-block:: text

   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │               Resolution Priority Order               │
   │                                                       │
   │  1. Session cache (versions found earlier)            │
   │          │ miss                                       │
   │          ▼                                            │
   │  2. Previous dependency graph (prior run)             │
   │          │ miss                                       │
   │          ▼                                            │
   │  3. Network (PyPI / GitHub / GitLab)                  │
   │     (per-package configurable)                        │
   │          │ age filter empties result                  │
   │          ▼                                            │
   │  4. Cache server fallback                             │
   │     (multiple_versions mode only)                     │
   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

   Git URL requirements (top-level only) bypass this
   chain entirely: the repo is cloned and the version
   is extracted from package metadata.

Versions discovered from any source are merged into the session cache.
Subsequent requests for the same package skip the network entirely if
the cache already contains a matching version.

Provider Hierarchy
------------------

All resolution sources inherit from ``BaseProvider``, which implements
the resolvelib ``ExtrasProvider`` interface.  The bootstrap engine and
CLI commands interact with providers through a common
``find_matches()`` method.

.. code-block:: text

   BaseProvider
   ├── PyPIProvider         (PEP 503 Simple API)
   │   └── PyPICacheProvider  (fromager's own wheel server)
   ├── GenericProvider      (callback-based, parses tags)
   │   ├── GitHubTagProvider
   │   └── GitLabTagProvider
   └── VersionMapProvider   (pre-resolved version→URL map)

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 75

   * - Provider
     - What it queries
   * - ``PyPIProvider``
     - Any PEP 503 Simple API index (pypi.org, custom mirrors).
       Filters by platform tags, Python version, and yanked status.
   * - ``PyPICacheProvider``
     - Subclass of ``PyPIProvider`` pointing at fromager's own wheel
       server.  No cooldown applied.  Used as a fallback when age
       filtering eliminates all candidates.
   * - ``GenericProvider``
     - Callback-based provider that pairs a version source function
       with a configurable match function (plain parse or regex).
       Base class for the tag providers below.
   * - ``GitHubTagProvider``
     - GitHub REST API for repository tags.  Versions are parsed
       from tag names using a configurable pattern.
   * - ``GitLabTagProvider``
     - GitLab REST API for repository tags.  Includes upload
       timestamps for age filtering.
   * - ``VersionMapProvider``
     - Wraps a pre-built ``VersionMap`` (version → URL mapping).
       Used when versions are already known, e.g. from a prior
       resolution or a settings-provided URL template.

Per-package settings in YAML can select which provider to use and
configure its parameters (index URL, tag pattern, etc.).  Override
plugins can replace the provider entirely for a specific package via
the ``get_resolver_provider`` hook.

Version Filtering Window
-------------------------

Two age-based filters can narrow the set of acceptable versions:

.. code-block:: text

   ◄── too old ──┤  acceptable window  ├── too new ──►

                 │                      │
            max_age cutoff         cooldown cutoff
          (reject before this)   (reject after this)

- **Cooldown** rejects releases that are too new.  It ensures a
  minimum time has passed since publication, guarding against
  problematic releases.  Configurable per package; bypassed for
  exact version pins (``==``).

- **Max age** rejects releases that are too old.  Used primarily in
  ``multiple_versions`` mode to limit the range of versions built.

.. versionchanged:: 0.84.0

   Packages with an explicit constraint bypass the max age filter in
   both modes.  All candidates must still satisfy the requirement,
   constraint, and cooldown policy.

For packages without constraints, when both filters are active, only
versions published within the window are considered.  If all candidates
are filtered out, the behavior depends
on the mode: in single-version mode a warning is logged and all
candidates are kept; in ``multiple_versions`` mode the cache server
fallback is tried instead.

Flat Resolution by Design
-------------------------

Fromager deliberately does **not** use resolvelib's transitive
dependency resolution.  Every provider's ``get_dependencies()`` method
returns an empty list.  This means resolution is a simple "find the
best matching version" operation, not a full constraint solver with
backtracking.

Transitive dependencies are handled by the bootstrap engine's own DFS
loop: after a package is built, its install dependencies are extracted
from the wheel metadata and pushed onto the work stack as new
``RESOLVE`` phase items.  This separation keeps the resolver stateless
and makes each resolution call independent and thread-safe.

Per-Package Configuration
-------------------------

Package settings files (YAML) can configure the resolver for each
package independently: resolver type (PyPI, GitHub tags, GitLab tags,
hook-based, or blocked), index URL, cooldown, tag pattern, and
override plugins.

See :doc:`package-settings` for how settings are loaded and merged.

# resolve any dependencies.

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime
import functools
import logging
import os
import re
import typing
from collections.abc import Iterable
from operator import attrgetter
from platform import python_version
from urllib.parse import quote, urlparse

import pypi_simple
import resolvelib
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.specifiers import InvalidSpecifier, SpecifierSet
from packaging.tags import Tag, sys_tags
from packaging.utils import (
    BuildTag,
    canonicalize_name,
    parse_wheel_filename,
)
from packaging.version import Version
from requests.models import Response
from resolvelib.resolvers import RequirementInformation

from . import overrides
from .candidate import Candidate, Cooldown
from .constraints import Constraints
from .downloads import extract_filename_from_url as extract_filename_from_url
from .extras_provider import ExtrasProvider
from .http_retry import RETRYABLE_EXCEPTIONS, retry_on_exception
from .request_session import session
from .requirements_file import RequirementType
from .versionmap import VersionMap

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from . import context


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

PYTHON_VERSION = Version(python_version())
DEBUG_RESOLVER = os.environ.get("DEBUG_RESOLVER", "")
PYPI_SERVER_URL = "https://pypi.org/simple"
GITHUB_URL = "https://github.com"

# all supported tags
SUPPORTED_TAGS: frozenset[Tag] = frozenset(sys_tags())
# same, but ignore the platform for 'ignore_platform' flag
IGNORE_PLATFORM: str = "ignore"
SUPPORTED_TAGS_IGNORE_PLATFORM: frozenset[Tag] = frozenset(
    Tag(t.interpreter, t.abi, IGNORE_PLATFORM) for t in SUPPORTED_TAGS
)


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=200)
def match_py_req(py_req: str, *, python_version: Version = PYTHON_VERSION) -> bool:
    """Python version requirement lookup with LRU cache

    Raises InvalidSpecifier on error

    SpecifierSet parsing and matching takes a non-trivial amount of time. A
    bootstrap run can spend over 10% of its time in parsing and matching
    Python version requirements.

    This function caches the result of SpecifierSet parsing and contains
    operation for Python version requirement. Most packages share similar
    constraints, e.g. ``>= 3.10``.
    """
    return python_version in SpecifierSet(py_req)


def resolve(
    *,
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool = True,
    include_wheels: bool = True,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> tuple[str, Version]:
    """Resolve requirement and return the best matching version.

    Returns (url, version) tuple for the highest matching version.
    """
    # Create the (reusable) resolver.
    provider = overrides.find_and_invoke(
        req.name,
        "get_resolver_provider",
        default_resolver_provider,
        ctx=ctx,
        req=req,
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )
    provider.cooldown = resolve_package_cooldown(ctx, req, req_type=req_type)
    max_age_cutoff = _compute_max_age_cutoff(ctx)
    results = find_all_matching_from_provider(
        provider, req, max_age_cutoff=max_age_cutoff
    )
    return results[0]


def default_resolver_provider(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool,
    include_wheels: bool,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> (
    PyPIProvider
    | GenericProvider
    | GitHubTagProvider
    | GitLabTagProvider
    | VersionMapProvider
):
    """Lookup resolver provider to resolve package versions"""
    return PyPIProvider(
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        constraints=ctx.constraints,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )


def _has_equality_pin(req: Requirement) -> bool:
    """Return True if the requirement has a single exact ``==`` pin.

    Rejects wildcard pins (``==1.*``) and compound specifiers (``==1,>2``)
    which are not true exact version pins.
    """
    specs = list(req.specifier)
    return len(specs) == 1 and specs[0].operator == "==" and "*" not in specs[0].version


def resolve_package_cooldown(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
) -> Cooldown | None:
    """Compute the effective cooldown for a single package.

    Args:
        ctx: The current work context (provides the global cooldown).
        req: The package requirement being resolved.
        req_type: The requirement type (top-level, install, etc.).

    Returns:
        The cooldown to pass to the provider, or ``None`` if disabled.
    """
    if req_type == RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL and _has_equality_pin(req):
        if ctx.cooldown is not None:
            logger.info("cooldown bypassed as the top-level requirement uses == pin")
        return None

    per_package_days = ctx.package_build_info(req).resolver_min_release_age
    global_cooldown = ctx.cooldown
    if per_package_days is None:
        return global_cooldown
    if per_package_days == 0:
        return None
    # Per-package positive override: inherit bootstrap_time from global so all
    # resolutions in a single run share the same fixed cutoff point.
    bootstrap_time = (
        global_cooldown.bootstrap_time
        if global_cooldown is not None
        else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
    )
    return Cooldown(
        min_age=datetime.timedelta(days=per_package_days),
        bootstrap_time=bootstrap_time,
    )

    Uses the cooldown's bootstrap_time for consistency across a single run.
    """

        return None

Skim it once, keep it handy, and refer back whenever you are unsure.\n\n> **Note**: If you're using AI coding assistants, also see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for AI-optimized quick reference.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [Quick Start](#quick-start)\n- [Coding Standards](#coding-standards)\n- [Testing](#testing)\n- [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines)\n- [Before Submitting](#before-submitting)\n- [Design Patterns Used in Fromager](#design-patterns-used-in-fromager)\n- [Quick Reference](#quick-reference)\n- [Getting Help](#getting-help)\n- [Resources](#resources)\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.12 or newer\n\n- `hatch` for environment and task management\n\n  ```bash\n  pip install hatch\n  # or\n  pipx install hatch  # recommended\n  ```\n\n### Initial Setup\n\n```bash\n# 1. Fork the repository on GitHub\n# 2. Clone your fork\ngit clone https://github.com/<your-username>/fromager.git\ncd fromager\n\n# 3. Add upstream remote\ngit remote add upstream https://github.com/python-wheel-build/fromager.git\n\n# 4. Create development environment\nhatch env create\n\n# 5. Install pre-commit hooks (optional but recommended)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n```\n\n### Contribution Workflow\n\n```bash\n# 1. Sync with upstream\ngit checkout main\ngit fetch upstream\ngit merge upstream/main\n\n# 2. Create a feature branch\ngit checkout -b feat/<short-description>\n\n# 3. Make changes and test as you go\nhatch run test:test tests/test_<module>.py       # Test your specific changes\n\n# 4. Before committing, run full quality checks\nhatch run lint:precommit\n\n# 5. Commit using Conventional Commits\ngit commit -m \"feat(scope): short summary\"\n\n# 6. Push to your fork\ngit push origin feat/<short-description>\n\n# 7. Create a pull request on GitHub\n```\n\n### Pre-commit Hook (Recommended)\n\nTo ensure quality checks run automatically before each commit, install the pre-commit hooks that run linting, mypy type checking, and commit message validation:\n\n```bash\n# Install pre-commit hooks (run once after cloning)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n\n# The hooks automatically run linters before each commit and validate\n# that commit messages follow Conventional Commits format.\n\n# If a hook fails, it will prevent the commit and show helpful messages.\n# You can fix formatting issues automatically with:\nhatch run lint:fix\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hooks prevent commits that would fail CI quality checks, and enforce that all commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format documented in the [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines) section.\n\n---\n\n## Coding Standards\n\n### Type Annotations\n\n- Every function (including tests) must annotate all parameters and return values.\n- Use modern `X | None` syntax instead of `Optional[X]` (PEP 604).\n- Prefer precise collection types (`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, etc.).\n\n```python\ndef process(data: str | None, count: int = 0) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Process the input and return aggregate counts.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n```\n\n### Code Quality and Formatting\n\n- Ruff enforces both formatting and linting.\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to automatically format code.\n- See [Quick Reference](#quick-reference) for additional commands.\n\n### Import Organization\n\n- **PEP 8: imports should be at the top**: All import statements must be placed at the top of the file, after module docstrings and before other code.\n- **No local imports**: Do not place import statements inside functions, methods, or conditional blocks.\n\n### Documentation Expectations\n\n- Add a module docstring describing purpose and high-level behavior.\n- Public functions and classes require docstrings that cover arguments, return values, and noteworthy behavior.\n- Keep prose short and imperative; explain \"why\" decisions when the code itself cannot.\n\n```python\ndef retry_on_exception(\n    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...],\n    max_attempts: int = 5,\n) -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Retry decorated call on the provided exception types.\n\n    Args:\n        exceptions: Exception types that trigger a retry.\n        max_attempts: Maximum number of attempts.\n\n    Returns:\n        Decorator function.\n    \"\"\"\n    ...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never repeat the code literally.\n\n```python\n# Bad - comment just repeats the code\nx = x + 1  # increment x\n\n# Good - clear variable name makes the comment unnecessary\ntotal_attempts += 1\n\n# Good - comment explains the reasoning behind the approach\n# Exponential backoff avoids thundering herd when many jobs retry at once.\nwait_time = min(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1), max_backoff)\n```\n\n### Logging\n\n- Use a module-level logger and the appropriate log level for the situation.\n- When processing per-requirement work, wrap nested calls in `req_ctxvar_context()` so log records automatically include the package (and optional version). This keeps CLI logs searchable even when work runs in parallel.\n\n```python\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\ndef sync_artifacts() -> None:\n    logger.info(\"Starting artifact sync\")\n    logger.debug(\"Artifacts queued: %s\", pending_jobs)\n\n# When processing a specific package, wrap calls to include package info in logs\n# req: Requirement object for the package being processed\n# version: Version string being built (optional)\nwith req_ctxvar_context(req, version):\n    logger.info(\"Resolving build dependencies\")  # Logs will include package name\n```\n\n### Error Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = load_config(config_file)\n    # Assert\n    assert result[\"setting\"] == \"value\"\n```\n\n### Useful Commands\n\n```bash\nhatch run test:test                              # Full suite\nhatch run test:test tests/test_context.py        # Specific file\nhatch run test:test --log-level DEBUG            # Verbose output\nhatch run test:coverage-report                   # Coverage summary\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commit Guidelines\n\nFromager follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/).\n\n```text\n<type>(<scope>): <short summary>\n\n<body explaining what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        return value.strip()\n    raise TypeError(f\"unsupported type {type(value)}: {value!r}\")\n\nEnvKey = typing.Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_validate_envkey)]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n| -- | -- |\n| Run tests | `hatch run test:test` |\n| Check code quality | `hatch run lint:check` |\n| Fix formatting | `hatch run lint:fix` |\n| Type checking | `hatch run mypy:check` |\n\n### Standards\n\n| Standard | Requirement |\n| -- | -- |\n| Type annotations | Required for every function |\n| Docstrings | Required on public APIs |\n| Tests | Required for new behavior |\n| Trailing whitespace | Forbidden |\n| File endings | Single newline |\n| Commit format | Conventional Commits |\n\n---\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for discussion or questions or design proposals.\n- File an issue with a minimal reproduction for bugs.\n- Ask for targeted feedback directly in your pull request.\n\n## Resources\n\n- [PEP 8 - Style Guide](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008/)\n- [PEP 484 - Type Hints](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0484/)\n- [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)\n- [pytest Documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [Ruff Documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)\n\n---\n\n**Thanks for contributing to Fromager!** If you spot gaps or have suggestions for this guide, open an issue or start a discussion—we love improving our contributor experience.\n# AI Agent Guide for Fromager\n\n> **Note**: This file is also available as `CLAUDE.md` (symlink) for Claude Code CLI users.\n>\n> **You MUST read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before writing code.** It contains coding standards, type annotation rules, design patterns, and commit message format. This file provides agent-specific quick reference only.\n\n## Essential Rules (MUST FOLLOW)\n\n### Do\n\n- Keep all written text concise and easy to understand — docstrings, comments, commit messages, PR descriptions, and documentation\n- Add docstrings on all public functions and classes\n- Use file-scoped commands for fast feedback (see below)\n- Follow existing patterns — search codebase for similar code\n- Chain exceptions: `raise ValueError(...) from err`\n- Use `req_ctxvar_context()` for per-requirement logging\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to format code\n- Always use `git commit --signoff`\n\n### Don't\n\n- Don't run full test suite for small changes (use file-scoped)\n- Don't create temporary helper scripts or workarounds\n- Don't commit without running quality checks\n- Don't make large speculative changes — ask first or propose a plan\n- Don't update git config or force push to main\n- Don't use bare `except:` — always specify exception types\n- Don't invent new patterns — search the codebase for existing ones\n\n## Commands (IMPORTANT: Use File-Scoped First)\n\n### Setup (Run Once)\n\n```bash\nhatch run lint:install-hooks    # Pre-commit hooks for automatic formatting\n```\n\n### File-Scoped (PREFER THESE)\n\n```bash\nhatch run mypy:check <filepath>                          # Type check single file\nhatch run lint:fix <filepath>                            # Format single file\nhatch run test:test tests/test_<module>.py               # Test specific file\nhatch run test:test tests/test_<module>.py::test_name    # Test specific function\nhatch run test:test <filepath> --log-level DEBUG         # Debug test\n```\n\n### Project-Wide (ASK BEFORE RUNNING)\n\n```bash\nhatch run lint:fix       # Format all code\nhatch run test:test      # Full test suite (slow!)\nhatch run mypy:check     # Type check everything\nhatch run lint:check     # Final lint check\nhatch run lint:precommit # All linters and pre-commit hooks\n```\n\n## Safety and Permissions\n\n### Allowed Without Asking\n\n- Read files, search codebase\n- Run file-scoped linting, type checking, tests\n- Edit existing files following established patterns\n- Create test files\n\n### Ask First\n\n- Installing/updating packages in pyproject.toml\n- Git commit or push operations\n- Deleting files or entire modules\n- Running full test suite\n- Creating new modules or major refactors\n- Making breaking changes\n\n## Project Structure\n\n- `src/fromager/` — Main package code\n- `tests/` — Unit tests (mirror `src/` structure)\n- `e2e/` — End-to-end integration tests\n- `docs/` — Sphinx documentation\n\n### Reference Files for Patterns\n\nLook at these before writing code:\n\n- Type annotations: `src/fromager/context.py`\n- Pydantic models: `src/fromager/packagesettings.py`\n- Logging with context: `src/fromager/resolver.py`\n- Error handling: `src/fromager/commands.py`\n- Testing patterns: `tests/test_context.py`\n\n## Code Patterns\n\n**Import rules:** All imports at the top of the file, no local imports. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for details.\n\n**URLs:** Use the `.test` TLD (e.g. `https://pkg.test/simple/`) instead of `example.com` in tests. Use `.example` TLD in examples.\n\n**Testing:** Use Arrange/Act/Assert pattern, name functions `test_<behavior>()`. See `tests/test_context.py` for examples.\n\n## Documentation and doc strings\n\n- Use single backticks around function and class names in markdown (e.g. `req_ctxvar_context()`, `WorkContext`), double backticks in .rst (reStructuredText)\n- Use Sphinx `versionadded`, `versionremoved`, `versionchanged` directives for user-facing changes (get next version from last git tag)\n- When code changes affect the architecture described in `docs/concepts/`, update the relevant doc:\n  - `architecture-overview.rst` — major subsystems, data flow, extension points, key data structures\n  - `bootstrapper-architecture.rst` — phase pipeline, class hierarchy, bootstrapper-phase interaction\n  - `resolver-architecture.rst` — resolution strategies, provider hierarchy, version filtering\n  - `hooks-and-overrides.rst` — override hook points, global hooks, plugin discovery\n  - `package-settings.rst` — settings loading flow, merge order, PackageBuildInfo facade\n\n## Commit Messages\n\nFollow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for format, types, and examples.\n\nUse backticks around function and class names (e.g. `WorkContext`)\n\nAlways use `--signoff` to add a DCO sign-off. When AI agents create or significantly modify code, also add attribution:\n\n```text\ngit commit --signoff -m \"feat(scope): short summary\n\nBody explaining what and why.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #123\n```\n\nThis produces a commit message with both the `Signed-off-by` trailer (from `--signoff`) and the `Co-Authored-By` trailer.\n\n## End-to-end tests\n\nThere is a set of end-to-end tests in `./e2e`. Files named like\n`test_*.sh` are test scripts and files named like `ci_*.sh` are CI\ntest suites that run the individual test scripts.\n\nThe end-to-end tests are expensive so **ONLY** run them when asked.\n\nThe CI test suites produce a lot of output. The most important\ninformation is in the summary at the end, where it shows which test\nscripts fail. Always run CI jobs in a way that only adds the last 25\nlines to the context window, then run an individual failing test\nscript to debug the problem.\n\n## Workflow for Complex Tasks\n\n1. **Search codebase** for similar patterns first\n2. **Create a checklist** for tracking progress\n3. **Work through items** one at a time\n4. **Run file-scoped tests** after each change\n5. **Run full quality checks** only at the end: `hatch run lint:fix && hatch run test:test && hatch run mypy:check && hatch run lint:check`\n\n---\n\n**See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for comprehensive standards, detailed examples, and design patterns.**\n---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n---\nname: surgical-patch\ndescription: Fix bugs and small behavior changes at the narrowest responsible layer. Use when regression proof, preserved surrounding behavior, and task-relevant tests matter.\n---\n\n# Surgical patch\n\nReproduce failure first when economical; otherwise capture strongest available evidence.\n\n- Trace symptom to responsible mechanism.\n- Change narrowest layer that owns incorrect behavior.\n- Preserve unrelated behavior and user changes.\n- Avoid cleanup, renaming, and abstraction outside fix.\n- Add only regression proof relevant to task.\n\nRun focused proof plus nearest affected gate. Stop when failure is fixed and regression proof passes.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
