tuple[str, Version]:\n    \"\"\"Resolve requirement and return the best matching version.\n\n    Returns (url, version) tuple for the highest matching version.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Create the (reusable) resolver.\n    provider = overrides.find_and_invoke(\n        req.name,\n        \"get_resolver_provider\",\n        default_resolver_provider,\n        ctx=ctx,\n        req=req,\n        include_sdists=include_sdists,\n        include_wheels=include_wheels,\n        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,\n        req_type=req_type,\n        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,\n    )\n    provider.cooldown = resolve_package_cooldown(ctx, req, req_type=req_type)\n    max_age_cutoff = _compute_max_age_cutoff(ctx)\n    results = find_all_matching_from_provider(\n        provider, req, max_age_cutoff=max_age_cutoff\n    )\n    return results[0]\n\n\ndef default_resolver_provider(\n    ctx: context.WorkContext,\n    req: Requirement,\n    sdist_server_url: str,\n    include_sdists: bool,\n    include_wheels: bool,\n    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,\n    ignore_platform: bool = False,\n) -> (\n    PyPIProvider\n    | GenericProvider\n    | GitHubTagProvider\n    | GitLabTagProvider\n    | VersionMapProvider\n):\n    \"\"\"Lookup resolver provider to resolve package versions\"\"\"\n    return PyPIProvider(\n        include_sdists=include_sdists,\n _has_equality_pin(req: Requirement) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Return True if the requirement has a single exact ``==`` pin.\n\n    Rejects wildcard pins (``==1.*``) and compound specifiers (``==1,>2``)\n    which are not true exact version pins.\n    \"\"\"\n    specs = list(req.specifier)\n    return len(specs) == 1 and specs[0].operator == \"==\" and \"*\" not in specs[0].version\n\n\ndef resolve_package_cooldown(\n    ctx: context.WorkContext,\n    req: Requirement,\n    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,\n) -> Cooldown | None:\n    \"\"\"Compute the effective cooldown for a single package.\n\n    Args:\n        ctx: The current work context (provides the global cooldown).\n        req: The package requirement being resolved.\n        req_type: The requirement type (top-level, install, etc.).\n\n    Returns:\n        The cooldown to pass to the provider, or ``None`` if disabled.\n    \"\"\"\n    if req_type == RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL and _has_equality_pin(req):\n        if ctx.cooldown is not None:\n            logger.info(\"cooldown bypassed as the top-level requirement uses == pin\")\n        return None\n\n    per_package_days = ctx.package_build_info(req).resolver_min_release_age\n    global_cooldown = ctx.cooldown\n    if per_package_days is None:\n        return global_cooldown\n    if per_package_days == 0:\n        return None\n    # Per-package positive override: inherit bootstrap_time from global so all\n    # resolutions in a single run share the same fixed cutoff point.\n    bootstrap_time = (\n        global_cooldown.bootstrap_time\n        if global_cooldown is not None\n        else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)\n    )\n    return Cooldown(\n        min_age=datetime.timedelta(days=per_package_days),\n        bootstrap_time=bootstrap_time,\n    )\n\n\ndef _compute_max_age_cutoff(\n    ctx: context.WorkContext,\n) -> datetime.datetime | None:\n    \"\"\"Compute the cutoff time for max release age filtering.\n\n    Returns the oldest acceptable upload time, or None if disabled.\n    Uses the cooldown's bootstrap_time for consistency across a single run.\n    \"\"\"\n    if ctx.max_release_age is None:\n        return None\n    bootstrap_time = (\n        ctx.cooldown.bootstrap_time\n        if ctx.cooldown is not None\n        else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)\n    )\n    return bootstrap_time - ctx.max_release_age\n\n\nclass LogReporter(resolvelib.BaseReporter):\n    \"\"\"Report resolution events\n\n    Implements part of the BaseReporter API to log a few events related to\n    resolving requirements.\n\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, req: Requirement):\n        self.req = req\n        super().__init__()\n\n    def _report(self, msg: str, *args: typing.Any) -> None:\n        logger.info(msg, *args)\n\n    def starting(self) -> None:\n        self._report(\"looking for candidates for %r\", self.req)\n\n    def rejecting_candidate(self, criterion: typing.Any, candidate: typing.Any) -> None:\n        self._report(\"resolver rejecting candidate %s: %s\", candidate, criterion)\n\n    def pinning(self, candidate: typing.Any) -> None:\n        self._report(\"selecting %s\", candidate)\n\n    def ending(self, state: typing.Any) -> None:\n        self._report(\"successfully resolved %r\", self.req)\n\n\ndef find_all_matching_from_provider(\n    provider: BaseProvider,\n    req: Requirement,\n    max_age_cutoff: datetime.datetime | None = None,\n    fallback_on_empty_age_filter: bool = True,\n) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n    \"\"\"Find all matching candidates from provider without full dependency resolution.\n\n    This function collects ALL candidates that match the requirement, rather than\n    performing full dependency resolution to find a single best candidate.\n\n    Args:\n        provider: The provider to query for candidates.\n        req: The requirement to match.\n        max_age_cutoff: If set, reject candidates published before this time.\n            If all candidates are older than the cutoff, all are kept and\n            a warning is emitted to avoid empty resolution.\n        fallback_on_empty_age_filter: If ``True`` (default), keep all\n            candidates when age filtering would produce an empty result.\n            If ``False``, return an empty list instead, allowing the\n            caller to implement its own fallback strategy.\n\n    Returns list of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).\n\n    IMPORTANT: This bypasses resolvelib's full resolver to collect all matching\n    candidates. This is safe ONLY because BaseProvider.get_dependencies() returns\n    an empty list (no transitive dependencies to resolve). The empty incompatibilities\n    dict means no version is ever excluded based on conflicts.\n\n    If get_dependencies() is ever extended to return actual dependencies, this\n    function must be revisited to use resolvelib's full resolution algorithm\n    (Resolver.resolve()) to properly handle dependency conflicts and backtracking.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Get all matching candidates directly from provider\n    # instead of using resolvelib's resolver which picks just one\n    identifier = provider.identify(req)\n    try:\n        # Bypass resolvelib's resolver to collect all matching candidates rather than\n        # just the single best one. This is safe because get_dependencies() returns []\n        # (no transitive deps to resolve). If get_dependencies() is ever extended,\n        # this must be revisited to use resolvelib's full resolution.\n        candidates = provider.find_matches(\n            identifier=identifier,\n            requirements={identifier: [req]},\n            incompatibilities={},  # Empty - safe only because no transitive deps\n        )\n    except resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException as err:\n        constraint = provider.constraints.get_constraint(req.name)\n        provider_desc = provider.get_provider_description()\n        original_msg = str(err)\n        raise resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException(\n            f\"Unable to resolve requirement specifier {req} with constraint {constraint} using {provider_desc}: {original_msg}\"\n        ) from err\n\n    # Materialize candidates so we can iterate more than once if filtering\n    candidates_list = list(candidates)\n\n    if max_age_cutoff is not None:\n        logger.info(\n            \"%s: found %d candidate(s) matching %s\",\n            req.name,\n            len(candidates_list),\n            req,\n        )\n        max_age_days = (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC) - max_age_cutoff).days\n        filtered = [\n            c\n            for c in candidates_list\n            if c.upload_time is None or c.upload_time >= max_age_cutoff\n        ]\n        dropped = len(candidates_list) - len(filtered)\n        if dropped:\n            logger.info(\n                \"%s: have %d candidate(s) of %s published within %d days\",\n                req.name,\n                len(filtered),\n                req,\n                max_age_days,\n            )\n        if filtered:\n            candidates_list = filtered\n        elif fallback_on_empty_age_filter:\n            logger.warning(\n                \"%s: all %d candidate(s) of %s are older than %d days, \"\n                \"keeping all to avoid empty resolution\",\n                req.name,\n                len(candidates_list),\n                req,\n                max_age_days,\n            )\n        else:\n            logger.info(\n                \"%s: all %d candidate(s) of %s are older than %d days\",\n                req.name,\n                len(candidates_list),\n                req,\n                max_age_days,\n            )\n            candidates_list = []\n\n    # Convert candidates to list of (url, version) tuples\n    # Candidates are sorted by version (highest first) by BaseProvider.find_matches()\n    # which calls sorted(candidates, key=attrgetter(\"version\", \"build_tag\"), reverse=True)\n    return [(c.url, c.version) for c in candidates_list]\n\n\ndef get_project_from_pypi(\n    project: str,\n    extras: typing.Iterable[str],\n    sdist_server_url: str,\n    ignore_platform: bool = False,\n    *,\n    override_download_url: str | None = None,\n) -> Candidates:\n    \"\"\"Fetch and filter package candidates from a PyPI-compatible server.\n\n    Filters the project's package list by: project status, filename\n    validity, package type (sdist/wheel), yanked status, Python version\n    compatibility, and platform tags. {"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_8","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc 'cat /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/caveman/SKILL.md /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/surgical-patch/SKILL.md'","aggregated_output":"---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n---\nname: surgical-patch\ndescription: Fix bugs and small behavior changes at the narrowest responsible layer. Use when regression proof, preserved surrounding behavior, and task-relevant tests matter.\n---\n\n# Surgical patch\n\nReproduce failure first when economical; otherwise capture strongest available evidence.\n\n- Trace symptom to responsible mechanism.\n- Change narrowest layer that owns incorrect behavior.\n- Preserve unrelated behavior and user changes.\n- Avoid cleanup, renaming, and abstraction outside fix.\n- Add only regression proof relevant to task.\n\nRun focused proof plus nearest affected gate. Stop when failure is fixed and regression proof passes.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Tag(t.interpreter, t.abi, IGNORE_PLATFORM) for t in SUPPORTED_TAGS\n)\n\n\n@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=200)\ndef match_py_req(py_req: str, *, python_version: Version = PYTHON_VERSION) -> bool:\n single package.\n\n    Args:\n        ctx: The current work context (provides the global cooldown).\n        req: The package requirement being resolved.\n        req_type: The requirement type (top-level, install, etc.).\n\n    Returns:\n        The cooldown to pass to the provider, or ``None`` if disabled.\n    \"\"\"\n    if req_type == RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL and _has_equality_pin(req):\n        if ctx.cooldown is not None:\n            logger.info(\"cooldown bypassed as the top-level requirement uses == pin\")\n        return None\n\n    per_package_days = ctx.package_build_info(req).resolver_min_release_age\n    global_cooldown = ctx.cooldown\n    if per_package_days is None:\n        return global_cooldown\n    if per_package_days == 0:\n        return None\n    # Per-package positive override: inherit bootstrap_time from global so all\n    # resolutions in a single run share the same fixed cutoff point.\n    bootstrap_time = (\n        global_cooldown.bootstrap_time\n        if global_cooldown is not None\n        else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)\n    )\n    return Cooldown(\n        min_age=datetime.timedelta(days=per_package_days),\n        bootstrap_time=bootstrap_time,\n    )\n\n\ndef _compute_max_age_cutoff(\n    ctx: context.WorkContext,\n) -> datetime.datetime | None:\n    \"\"\"Compute the cutoff time for max release age filtering.\n\n    Returns the oldest acceptable upload time, or None if disabled.\n    Uses the cooldown's bootstrap_time for consistency across a single run.\n    \"\"\"\n    if ctx.max_release_age is None:\n        return None\n    bootstrap_time = (\n        ctx.cooldown.bootstrap_time\n        if ctx.cooldown is not None\n        else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)\n    )\n    return bootstrap_time - ctx.max_release_age\n\n\nclass LogReporter(resolvelib.BaseReporter):\n    \"\"\"Report resolution events\n\n    Implements part of the BaseReporter API to log a few events related to\n    resolving requirements.\n\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, req: Requirement):\n        self.req = req\n        super().__init__()\n\n    def _report(self, msg: str, *args: typing.Any) -> None:\n        logger.info(msg, *args)\n\n    def starting(self) -> None:\n        self._report(\"looking for candidates for %r\", self.req)\n\n    def rejecting_candidate(self, criterion: typing.Any, candidate: typing.Any) -> None:\n        self._report(\"resolver rejecting candidate %s: %s\", candidate, criterion)\n\n    def pinning(self, candidate: typing.Any) -> None:\n        self._report(\"selecting %s\", candidate)\n\n    def ending(self, state: typing.Any) -> None:\n        self._report(\"successfully resolved %r\", avoid empty resolution.\n        fallback_on_empty_age_filter: If ``True`` (default), keep all\n            candidates when age filtering would produce an empty result.\n            If ``False``, safe only because no transitive deps\n        )\n    except resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException as err:\n        constraint = provider.constraints.get_constraint(req.name)\n        provider_desc = provider.get_provider_description()\n        original_msg = str(err)\n        raise resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException(\n            f\"Unable to resolve requirement specifier {req} with constraint {constraint} using {provider_desc}: {original_msg}\"\n        ) from err\n\n    # Materialize candidates so we can iterate more than once if filtering\n    candidates_list = list(candidates)\n\n    if max_age_cutoff is not None:\n        logger.info(\n            \"%s: found %d candidate(s) matching %s\",\n            req.name,\n            len(candidates_list),\n            req,\n        )\n        max_age_days = (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC) - Can substitute\n    ``override_download_url`` into each candidate's URL.\nimport logging\nimport pathlib\nimport typing\nfrom collections.abc import Generator\n\nfrom packaging.requirements import Requirement\nfrom packaging.specifiers import SpecifierSet\nfrom packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name\nfrom packaging.version import Version\n\nfrom . import requirements_file\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\ndef _is_blocked_specifier(specifier: SpecifierSet) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Return True if specifier blocks a package entirely.\n\n    The convention ``<0``, ``<0.0``, or ``<0.0.0`` is used to mark a\n    package as blocked so that no version can satisfy the constraint.\n    \"\"\"\n    specs = list(specifier)\n    return (\n        len(specs) == 1\n        and specs[0].operator == \"<\"\n        and Version(specs[0].version) == Version(\"0\")\n    )\n\n\nclass InvalidConstraintError(ValueError):\n    pass\n\n\nclass Constraints:\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        # mapping of canonical names to requirements\n        # NOTE: Requirement.name is not normalized\n        self._data: dict[NormalizedName, Requirement] = {}\n\n    def __iter__(self) -> Generator[NormalizedName, None, None]:\n        yield from self._data\n\n    def __bool__(self) -> bool:\n        return bool(self._data)\n\n    def __len__(self) -> int:\n        return len(self._data)\n\n    def add_constraint(self, unparsed: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add new constraint, must not conflict with any existing constraints\n\n        .. versionchanged: 0.83.0\n           Non-conflicting constraints are now combined. Constraints with\n           conflicts now raise :exc:`InvalidConstraintError`. Inputs without a\n           version specifier or with extras are also refused.\n        \"\"\"\n        req = Requirement(unparsed)\n        canon_name = canonicalize_name(req.name)\n        previous = self._data.get(canon_name)\n\n        # validator properties: must have a specifier, must not have extras or URL\n        if req.extras:\n            raise InvalidConstraintError(f\"Constraint {unparsed!r} has extras\")\n        if req.url:\n            raise InvalidConstraintError(f\"Constraint {unparsed!r} has a URL\")\n        if not req.specifier:\n            raise InvalidConstraintError(f\"Constraint {unparsed!r} has no specifiers\")\n\n        # A \"blocked\" specifier (<0, <0.0, <0.0.0) is intentionally\n        # unsatisfiable and used to exclude a package from builds.\n        blocked = _is_blocked_specifier(req.specifier)\n\n        # verify that incoming constraint is okay by itself\n        if not blocked and req.specifier.is_unsatisfiable():\n            raise InvalidConstraintError(f\"Constraint {unparsed!r} is unsatisfiable\")\n\n        if not requirements_file.evaluate_marker(req, req):\n            logger.debug(f\"Constraint {req} does not match environment\")\n            return\n\n        if previous is not None:\n            prev_blocked = _is_blocked_specifier(previous.specifier)\n            if blocked != prev_blocked:\n                raise InvalidConstraintError(\n                    f\"Cannot combine blocked and non-blocked constraints \"\n                    f\"(existing: {previous}, new: {req})\"\n                )\n            if not blocked:\n                logger.debug(\"combining constraints %s and %s\", previous, req)\n                new_specifier = req.specifier & previous.specifier\n                if new_specifier.is_unsatisfiable():\n                    raise InvalidConstraintError(\n                        f\"Combined specifier '{new_specifier}' is not satisfiable \"\n                        f\"(existing: {previous}, new: {req})\"\n                    )\n                req.specifier = new_specifier\n        else:\n            logger.debug(f\"adding constraint {req}\")\n\n        self._data[canon_name] = req\n\n    def load_constraints_file(self, constraints_file: str | pathlib.Path) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Load constraints from a constraints file or URL\"\"\"\n        logger.info(\"loading constraints from %s\", constraints_file)\n        content = requirements_file.parse_requirements_file(constraints_file)\n        for line in content:\n            self.add_constraint(line)\n\n    def dump_constraints(self, output: typing.TextIO) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Dump combined constraints to a text stream\"\"\"\n        # sort by normalized name\n        for _, req in sorted(self._data.items()):\n            # write requirement without markers. They have been evaluated\n            # in add_constraint()\n            output.write(f\"{req.name}{req.specifier}\\n\")\n\n    def get_constraint(self, name: str) -> Requirement | None:\n        return self._data.get(canonicalize_name(name))\n\n    def allow_prerelease(self, pkg_name: str) -> bool:\n        constraint = self.get_constraint(pkg_name)\n        if constraint:\n            return bool(constraint.specifier.prereleases)\n        return False\n\n    def is_blocked(self, pkg_name: str) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Return True if the package is blocked by a ``<0`` constraint.\"\"\"\n        constraint = self.get_constraint(pkg_name)\n        if constraint:\n            return _is_blocked_specifier(constraint.specifier)\n        return False\n\n    def is_satisfied_by(self, pkg_name: str, version: Version) -> bool:\n        constraint = self.get_constraint(pkg_name)\n        if constraint:\n            return constraint.specifier.contains(version, prereleases=True)\n        return True\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Architecture\n=====================\n\nFromager resolves package versions from multiple sources using a\nprovider abstraction.  This document describes the resolution\nstrategies, filtering, and key design decisions.\n\n.. seealso::\n\n   :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.\n   :doc:`bootstrapper-architecture` covers how resolution fits into the\n   bootstrap pipeline.\n\nResolution Strategies\n---------------------\n\nDuring bootstrap, the resolver coordinator tries these sources in\npriority order and accumulates results in a thread-safe session cache:\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n   │               Resolution Priority Order               │\n   │                                                       │\n   │  1. Session cache (versions found earlier)            │\n   │          │ miss                                       │\n   │          ▼                                            │\n   │  2. Previous dependency graph (prior run)             │\n   │          │ miss                                       │\n   │          ▼                                            │\n   │  3. Network (PyPI / GitHub / GitLab)                  │\n   │     (per-package configurable)                        │\n   │          │ age filter empties result                  │\n   │          ▼                                            │\n   │  4. Cache server fallback                             │\n   │     (multiple_versions mode only)                     │\n   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n\n   Git URL requirements (top-level only) bypass this\n   chain entirely: the repo is cloned and the version\n   is extracted from package metadata.\n\nVersions discovered from any source are merged into the session cache.\nSubsequent requests for the same package skip the network entirely if\nthe cache already contains a matching version.\n\nProvider Hierarchy\n------------------\n\nAll resolution sources inherit from ``BaseProvider``, which implements\nthe resolvelib ``ExtrasProvider`` interface.  The bootstrap engine and\nCLI commands interact with providers through a common\n``find_matches()`` method.\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   BaseProvider\n   ├── PyPIProvider         (PEP 503 Simple API)\n   │   └── PyPICacheProvider  (fromager's own wheel server)\n   ├── GenericProvider      (callback-based, parses tags)\n   │   ├── GitHubTagProvider\n   │   └── GitLabTagProvider\n   └── VersionMapProvider   (pre-resolved version→URL map)\n\n.. list-table::\n   :header-rows: 1\n   :widths: 25 75\n\n   * - Provider\n     - What it queries\n   * - ``PyPIProvider``\n     - Any PEP 503 Simple API index (pypi.org, custom mirrors).\n       Filters by platform tags, Python version, and yanked status.\n   * - ``PyPICacheProvider``\n     - Subclass of ``PyPIProvider`` pointing at fromager's own wheel\n       server.  No cooldown applied.  Used as a fallback when age\n       filtering eliminates all candidates.\n   * - ``GenericProvider``\n     - Callback-based provider that pairs a version source function\n       with a configurable match function (plain parse or regex).\n       Base class for the tag providers below.\n   * - ``GitHubTagProvider``\n     - GitHub REST API for repository tags.  Versions are parsed\n       from tag names using a configurable pattern.\n   * - ``GitLabTagProvider``\n     - GitLab REST API for repository tags.  Includes upload\n       timestamps for age filtering.\n   * - ``VersionMapProvider``\n     - Wraps a pre-built ``VersionMap`` (version → URL mapping).\n       Used when versions are already known, e.g. from a prior\n       resolution or a settings-provided URL template.\n\nPer-package settings in YAML can select which provider to use and\nconfigure its parameters (index URL, tag pattern, etc.).  Override\nplugins can replace the provider entirely for a specific package via\nthe ``get_resolver_provider`` hook.\n\nVersion Filtering Window\n-------------------------\n\nTwo age-based filters can narrow the set of acceptable versions:\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   ◄── too old ──┤  acceptable window  ├── too new ──►\n\n                 │                      │\n            max_age cutoff         cooldown cutoff\n          (reject before this)   (reject after this)\n\n- **Cooldown** rejects releases that are too new.  It ensures a\n  minimum time has passed since publication, guarding against\n  problematic releases.  Configurable per package; bypassed for\n  exact version pins (``==``).\n\n- **Max age** rejects releases that are too old.  Used primarily in\n  ``multiple_versions`` mode to limit the range of versions built.\n\nWhen both are active, only versions published within the window are\nconsidered.  If all candidates are filtered out, the behavior depends\non the mode: in single-version mode a warning is logged and all\ncandidates are kept; in ``multiple_versions`` mode the cache server\nfallback is tried instead.\n\nFlat Resolution by Design\n-------------------------\n\nFromager deliberately does **not** use resolvelib's transitive\ndependency resolution.  Every provider's ``get_dependencies()`` method\nreturns an empty list.  This means resolution is a simple \"find the\nbest matching version\" operation, not a full constraint solver with\nbacktracking.\n\nTransitive dependencies are handled by the bootstrap engine's own DFS\nloop: after a package is built, its install dependencies are extracted\nfrom the wheel metadata and pushed onto the work stack as new\n``RESOLVE`` phase items.  This separation keeps the resolver stateless\nand makes each resolution call independent and thread-safe.\n\nPer-Package Configuration\n-------------------------\n\nPackage settings files (YAML) can configure the resolver for each\npackage independently: resolver type (PyPI, GitHub tags, GitLab tags,\nhook-based, or blocked), index URL, cooldown, tag pattern, and\noverride plugins.\n\nSee :doc:`package-settings` for how settings are loaded and merged.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

"""Tests for the release-age cooldown policy (issue #877).

The cooldown rejects package versions published fewer than N days ago,
protecting against supply-chain attacks where a malicious version is
published and immediately pulled in by automated builds.
"""

import datetime
import logging
import pathlib
import re
import typing

import pytest
import requests_mock
import resolvelib
import yaml
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import (
    candidate,
    constraints,
    context,
    packagesettings,
    resolver,
    sources,
    wheels,
)
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

_BOOTSTRAP_TIME = datetime.datetime(2026, 3, 26, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS = datetime.timedelta(days=7)
# cutoff = 2026-03-19T00:00:00Z

# Use PEP 691 JSON format — pypi_simple reliably parses upload-time from JSON.
_PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json"

# Three versions at known ages:
#   2.0.0  uploaded 2026-03-24 →  2 days old (within cooldown)
#   1.3.2  uploaded 2026-03-15 → 11 days old (outside cooldown)
#   1.2.2  uploaded 2026-01-01 → 84 days old (outside cooldown)
_cooldown_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-15T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "ccc"},
            "upload-time": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_all_recent_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-25T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_COOLDOWN = candidate.Cooldown(
    min_age=_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS,
    bootstrap_time=_BOOTSTRAP_TIME,
)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clear_resolver_cache() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:
    """Clear the class-level resolver cache before each test.

    BaseProvider.resolver_cache is a ClassVar that persists across test
    instances. Without clearing it, candidates fetched in one test are reused
    by subsequent tests, bypassing mocked HTTP responses and producing
    incorrect results.
    """
    resolver.BaseProvider.clear_cache()
    resolver.BaseProvider._cooldown_unsupported_warned.clear()
    yield


def test_cooldown_filters_recent_version(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Versions within the cooldown window are skipped; older ones are selected."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
            result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        # 2.0.0 is 2 days old (within cooldown); 1.3.2 is 11 days old (outside).
        assert str(candidate.version) == "1.3.2"
        # 2.0.0 should be logged as blocked; 1.3.2 should not appear in the summary.
        assert "cooldown blocked 1 version(s): 2.0.0" in caplog.text


def test_cooldown_disabled_selects_latest() -> None:
    """Without a cooldown the resolver selects the latest version as normal."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=None)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        assert str(candidate.version) == "2.0.0"


def test_cooldown_all_blocked_raises_informative_error() -> None:
    """When all candidates are within the cooldown window the error says so."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_all_recent_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())

        with pytest.raises(resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException) as exc_info:
            rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        msg = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "2 candidate(s)" in msg
        assert "published within the last 7 days (release-age cooldown" in msg


def test_cooldown_rejects_candidate_without_upload_time(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """A candidate with no upload_time is rejected when a cooldown is active (fail closed)."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    candidate = resolver.Candidate(
        name="test-pkg",
        version=Version("1.0.0"),
        url="https://example.com/test-pkg-1.0.0.tar.gz",
        upload_time=None,
    )
    provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(cooldown=_COOLDOWN)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
        result = provider.is_blocked_by_cooldown(candidate)

    assert result is True
    assert "upload_time unknown" in caplog.text
    assert "1.0.0" in caplog.text

  \ Enrichment must happen before the error is\n  recorded in test mode or multiple-versions mode, and before the normal-mode raise.\n\nAdd tests to `tests/test_bootstrapper_iterative.py` and run that file.\n"

from __future__ import annotations

import concurrent.futures
import contextlib
import datetime
import json
import logging
import operator
import pathlib
import shutil
import tempfile
import typing

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version
from resolvelib.resolvers import ResolverException

from .. import (
    bootstrap_requirement_resolver,
    build_environment,
    dependencies,
    gitutils,
    progress,
    sources,
)
from ..dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from ..log import req_ctxvar_context, requirement_ctxvar
from ..requirements_file import RequirementType, SourceType
from . import _cache
from ._build import Build
from ._phase import Phase
from ._prepare_build import PrepareBuild
from ._prepare_source import PrepareSource
from ._process_install_deps import ProcessInstallDeps
from ._resolve import Resolve
from ._types import (
    _DEFAULT_BG_THREADS,
    FailureRecord,
    FailureType,
    SeenKey,
    SourceBuildResult,
)
from ._work_item import WorkItem

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .. import context

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class Bootstrapper:
    def __init__(
        self,
        ctx: context.WorkContext,
        progressbar: progress.Progressbar | None = None,
        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,
        cache_wheel_server_url: str | None = None,
        sdist_only: bool = False,
        test_mode: bool = False,
        multiple_versions: bool = False,
        num_bg_threads: int = _DEFAULT_BG_THREADS,
    ) -> None:
        if test_mode and sdist_only:
            raise ValueError(
                "--test-mode requires full wheel builds; incompatible with --sdist-only"
            )

        self.ctx = ctx
        self.progressbar = progressbar or progress.Progressbar(None)
        self.prev_graph = prev_graph
        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url or ctx.wheel_server_url
        self.sdist_only = sdist_only
        self.test_mode = test_mode
        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions
        self.why: list[tuple[RequirementType, Requirement, Version]] = []
        self._num_bg_threads = max(1, num_bg_threads)
        self._bg_pool: concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor | None = (
            concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(
                max_workers=self._num_bg_threads, thread_name_prefix="fromager-bg"
            )
        )

        # Delegate resolution to BootstrapRequirementResolver
        self._resolver = bootstrap_requirement_resolver.BootstrapRequirementResolver(
            ctx=ctx,
            prev_graph=prev_graph,
            multiple_versions=multiple_versions,
            cache_wheel_server_url=self.cache_wheel_server_url,
        )
        # Push items onto the stack as we start to resolve their
        # dependencies so at the end we have a list of items that need to
        # be built in order.
        self._build_stack: list[typing.Any] = []
        self._build_requirements: set[tuple[NormalizedName, str]] = set()

        # Track requirements we've seen before so we don't resolve the
        # same dependencies over and over and so we can break cycles in
        # the dependency list. The key is the requirements spec, rather
        # than the package, in case we do have multiple rules for the same
        # package.
        self._seen_requirements: set[SeenKey] = set()

        self._build_order_filename = self.ctx.work_dir / "build-order.json"
        self._stack_filename = self.ctx.work_dir / "bootstrap-stack.json"
        logger.info("recording bootstrap stack state to %s", self._stack_filename)

        # Track failed packages in test mode (list of typed dicts for JSON export)
        self.failed_packages: list[FailureRecord] = []

        # Track failed versions in multiple_versions mode
        self._failed_versions: dict[tuple[str, str], Exception] = {}

    @property
    def resolver(self) -> bootstrap_requirement_resolver.BootstrapRequirementResolver:
        """Public accessor for the version resolver."""
        return self._resolver

    def has_failed_version(self, pkg_name: NormalizedName, version: Version) -> bool:
        """Return True if this (pkg_name, version) has previously failed resolution."""
        return (pkg_name, str(version)) in self._failed_versions

    def _resolve_and_add_top_level(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
    ) -> tuple[str, Version] | None:
        """Resolve a top-level requirement and add it to the dependency graph.

        Private method called only by ``bootstrap()``.

        This is the pre-resolution phase before recursive bootstrapping begins.
        In test mode, catches resolution errors and records them as failures.

        When multiple_versions is enabled, resolves and adds all matching versions
        to the graph, but still returns only the first (highest) version for
        backward compatibility.

        Args:
            req: The top-level requirement to resolve.

        Returns:
            Tuple of (source_url, version) if resolution succeeded, None if it
            failed in test mode.

        Raises:
            Exception: In normal mode, re-raises any resolution error.
        """
        try:
            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)
            results = self.resolve_versions(
                req=req,
                req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
                parent_req=None,
                return_all_versions=self.multiple_versions,
            )
            if self.multiple_versions:
                logger.info(f"resolved {len(results)} version(s) for {req}")

            # Add all resolved versions to the graph
            for source_url, version in results:
                logger.info("%s resolves to %s", req, version)
                self.ctx.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
                    parent_name=None,
                    parent_version=None,
                    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
                    req=req,
                    req_version=version,
                    download_url=source_url,
                    pre_built=pbi.pre_built,
                    constraint=self.ctx.constraints.get_constraint(req.name),
                )

            if not results:
                if self.multiple_versions:
                    err = RuntimeError(f"no versions found for {req}")
                    self._record_failed_version(
                        req, "unresolved", err, "no versions resolved, skipping"
                    )
                    if self.test_mode:
                        self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
                    return None
                raise RuntimeError(f"Could not resolve any versions for {req}")

            # Return first result for backward compatibility
            return results[0]
        except Exception as err:
            if self.multiple_versions:
                self._record_failed_version(req, "unresolved", err, "failed to resolve")
                if self.test_mode:
                    self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
                return None
            if not self.test_mode:
                raise
            self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
            return None

        req_type: RequirementType,

This file provides agent-specific quick reference only.\n\n## Essential Rules (MUST FOLLOW)\n\n### Do\n\n- Keep all written text concise and easy to understand — docstrings, comments, commit messages, PR descriptions, and documentation\n- Add docstrings on all public functions and classes\n- Use file-scoped commands for fast feedback (see below)\n- Follow existing patterns — search codebase for similar code\n- Chain exceptions: `raise ValueError(...) from err`\n- Use `req_ctxvar_context()` for per-requirement logging\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to format code\n- Always use `git commit --signoff`\n\n### Don't\n\n- Don't run full test suite for small changes (use file-scoped)\n- Don't create temporary helper scripts or workarounds\n- Don't commit without running quality checks\n- Don't make large speculative changes — ask first or propose a plan\n- Don't update git config or force push to main\n- Don't use bare `except:` — always specify exception types\n- Don't invent new patterns — search the codebase for existing ones\n\n## Commands (IMPORTANT: Use File-Scoped First)\n\n### Setup (Run Once)\n\n```bash\nhatch run lint:install-hooks    # Pre-commit hooks for automatic formatting\n```\n\n### File-Scoped (PREFER THESE)\n\n```bash\nhatch run mypy:check <filepath>                          # Type check single file\nhatch run lint:fix <filepath>                            # Format single file\nhatch run test:test tests/test_<module>.py               # Test specific file\nhatch run test:test tests/test_<module>.py::test_name    # Test specific function\nhatch run test:test <filepath> --log-level DEBUG         # Debug test\n```\n\n### Project-Wide (ASK BEFORE RUNNING)\n\n```bash\nhatch run lint:fix       # Format all code\nhatch run test:test      # Full test suite (slow!)\nhatch run mypy:check     # Type check everything\nhatch run lint:check     # Final lint check\nhatch run lint:precommit # All linters and pre-commit hooks\n```\n\n## Safety and Permissions\n\n### Allowed Without Asking\n\n- Read files, search codebase\n- Run file-scoped linting, type checking, tests\n- Edit existing files following established patterns\n- Create test files\n\n### Ask First\n\n- Installing/updating packages in pyproject.toml\n- Git commit or push operations\n- Deleting files or entire modules\n- Running full test suite\n- Creating new modules or major refactors\n- Making breaking changes\n\n## Project Structure\n\n- `src/fromager/` — Main package code\n- `tests/` — Unit tests (mirror `src/` structure)\n- `e2e/` — End-to-end integration tests\n- `docs/` — Sphinx documentation\n\n### Reference Files for Patterns\n\nLook at these before writing code:\n\n- Type annotations: `src/fromager/context.py`\n- Pydantic models: `src/fromager/packagesettings.py`\n- Logging with context: `src/fromager/resolver.py`\n- Error handling: `src/fromager/commands.py`\n- Testing patterns: `tests/test_context.py`\n\n## Code Patterns\n\n**Import rules:** All imports at the top of the file, no local imports. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for details.\n\n**URLs:** Use the `.test` TLD (e.g. `https://pkg.test/simple/`) instead of `example.com` in tests. When AI agents create or significantly modify code, also add attribution:\n\n```text\ngit commit --signoff -m \"feat(scope): short summary\n\nBody explaining what and why.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #123\n```\n\nThis produces a commit message with both the `Signed-off-by` trailer (from `--signoff`) and the `Co-Authored-By` trailer.\n\n## End-to-end tests\n\nThere is a set of end-to-end tests in `./e2e`. Always run CI jobs in a way that only adds the last 25\nlines to the context window, then run an individual failing test\nscript to debug the problem.\n\n## Workflow for Complex Tasks\n\n1. **Search codebase** for similar patterns first\n2. **Create a checklist** for tracking progress\n3. **Work through items** one at a time\n4. **Run file-scoped tests** after each change\n5. **Run full quality checks** only at the end: `hatch run lint:fix && hatch run test:test && hatch run mypy:check && hatch run lint:check`\n\n---\n\n**See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for comprehensive standards, detailed examples, and design patterns.**\n# Contributing to Fromager\n\nFromager thrives on practical, well-tested contributions. etc.).\n\n```python\ndef process(data: str | None, count: int = 0) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Process the input and return aggregate counts.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n```\n\n### Code Quality and Organization\n\n- **PEP 8: imports should be at the top**: All import statements must be placed at the top of the file, after module docstrings and before other code.\n- **No local imports**: Do not place import statements inside functions, methods, or conditional blocks.\n\n### Documentation Expectations\n\n- Add a module docstring describing purpose and high-level behavior.\n- Public functions and classes require docstrings that cover arguments, return values, and noteworthy behavior.\n- Keep prose short and imperative; explain \"why\" decisions when the code itself cannot.\n\n```python\ndef retry_on_exception(\n    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...],\n    max_attempts: int = 5,\n) -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Retry decorated call on the provided exception ...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never repeat the code literally.\n\n```python\n# Bad - comment just repeats the code\nx = x + 1  # increment x\n\n# Good - clear variable name makes the comment unnecessary\ntotal_attempts += 1\n\n# Good - comment explains the reasoning behind the approach\n# Exponential backoff avoids thundering herd when many jobs retry at once.\nwait_time = min(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1), log records automatically include the package (and optional version). This keeps CLI logs searchable even when work runs in parallel.\n\n```python\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\ndef sync_artifacts() -> None:\n    logger.info(\"Starting artifact sync\")\n what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        return value.strip()\n    raise TypeError(f\"unsupported type {type(value)}: {value!r}\")\n\nEnvKey = typing.Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_validate_envkey)]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n| -- | -- |\n| Run tests | `hatch run test:test` |\n| Check code quality | `hatch run lint:check` |\n| Fix formatting | `hatch run lint:fix` |\n| Type checking | `hatch run mypy:check` |\n\n### Standards\n\n| Standard | Requirement |\n| -- | -- |\n| Type annotations | Required for every function |\n| Docstrings | Required on public APIs |\n| Tests | Required for new behavior |\n| Trailing whitespace | Forbidden |\n| File endings | Single newline |\n| Commit format | Conventional Commits |\n\n---\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for discussion or questions or design proposals.\n- File an issue with a minimal reproduction for bugs.\n- Ask for targeted feedback directly in your pull request.\n\n## Resources\n\n- [PEP 8 - Style Guide](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008/)\n- [PEP 484 - Type Hints](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0484/)\n- [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)\n- [pytest Documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [Ruff Documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)\n\n---\n\n**Thanks for contributing to Fromager!** If you spot gaps or have suggestions for this guide, open an issue or start a discussion—we love improving our contributor experience.\n---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

{"type":"item.started","item":{"id":"item_9","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc 'cat /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/caveman/SKILL.md'","aggregated_output":"","exit_code":null,"status":"in_progress"}}
{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_9","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc 'cat /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/caveman/SKILL.md'","aggregated_output":"---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

and resolved_version, then\n    creates new items at the START phase for each resolved version.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    # Identity (set at creation)\n    req: Requirement\n    req_type: RequirementType\n None = None\n    resolved_version: Version | None = None\n\n    build_sdist_only: bool = False\n\n    # Accumulated state (populated during phases)\n    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | set[Requirement] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=set)\n    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=set)\n\n    def is_build_requirement_context(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Return True if this item is being processed as part of a build requirement.\n\n        A package is a build dependency if its own requirement type is\n        build_system, build_backend, or build_sdist, OR if it is an install\n        requirement of something that is itself a build dependency (checked\n        by walking the ``why_snapshot`` chain).\n        \"\"\"\n        if       logger.debug(\n                \"is not an install requirement, not checking dependency chain for a build requirement\"\n            )\n            return False\n        for req_type, req, resolved_version in reversed(self.why_snapshot):\n            if req_type.is_build_requirement:\n                logger.debug(\n                    f\"is a build requirement because {req_type} dependency {req} ({resolved_version}) depends on it\"\n                )\n                return True\n        logger.debug(\"is not a build requirement\")\n        return False\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

"""Tests for the iterative bootstrap implementation.

Tests cover:
- Phase class hierarchy: class variables and base class behavior
- WorkItem dataclass defaults and state accumulation
- _track_why context manager behavior
- create_unresolved_work_items helper
- Resolve.run() version expansion
- Start.run() graph addition and seen-check
- PrepareSource.run() all branches (prebuilt, source, cached, bad path)
- PrepareBuild.run() dep installation and extraction
- Build.run() conditional install and result construction
- ProcessInstallDeps.run() hooks, dep extraction, error modes
- Complete.run() cleanup
- _handle_phase_error for all three error modes
- End-to-end iterative loop with LIFO ordering
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import concurrent.futures
import pathlib
import typing
from unittest.mock import Mock, call, patch

import pytest
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version
from resolvelib.resolvers import ResolverException

from fromager import bootstrapper, build_environment
from fromager.bootstrapper._build import Build
from fromager.bootstrapper._complete import Complete
from fromager.bootstrapper._phase import Phase
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_build import PrepareBuild

def _make_resolved_future(
    result: typing.Any,
) -> concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any]:
    """Return an already-completed Future carrying *result*."""
    future: concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any] = concurrent.futures.Future()
    future.set_result(result)
    return future


def _make_work_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
    source_url: str | None = None,
    version: str | None = None,
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> WorkItem:
    return WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=req_type,
        why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
        parent=parent,
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version) if version else None,
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )


def _make_resolve_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Resolve:
    return Resolve(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
        )
    )


def _make_start_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    version: str = "1.0",
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Start:
    return Start(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
            source_url=source_url,
            resolved_version=Version(version),
        )
    )


_PHASE_TO_CLASS: dict[BootstrapPhase, type[Phase]] = {
    BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE: Resolve,
    BootstrapPhase.START: Start,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE: PrepareSource,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD: PrepareBuild,
    BootstrapPhase.BUILD: Build,
    BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS: ProcessInstallDeps,
    BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE: Complete,
}


def _make_build_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    version: str = "1.0",
    phase: BootstrapPhase = BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,

    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> Phase:
    wi = WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        why_snapshot=[],
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version),
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )
    return _PHASE_TO_CLASS[phase](wi)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class Bootstrapper:
    def __init__(
        self,
        ctx: context.WorkContext,
        progressbar: progress.Progressbar | None = None,
        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,
        cache_wheel_server_url: str | None = None,
        sdist_only: bool = False,
        test_mode: bool = False,
        multiple_versions: bool = False,
        num_bg_threads: int = _DEFAULT_BG_THREADS,
    ) -> None:
        if test_mode and sdist_only:
            raise ValueError(
                "--test-mode requires full wheel builds; incompatible with --sdist-only"
            )

        self.ctx = ctx
        self.progressbar = progressbar or progress.Progressbar(None)
        self.prev_graph = prev_graph
        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url or ctx.wheel_server_url
        self.sdist_only = sdist_only
        self.test_mode = test_mode
        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions
        self.why: list[tuple[RequirementType, Requirement, Version]] = []
        self._num_bg_threads = max(1, num_bg_threads)
        self._bg_pool: concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor | None = (
            concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(
                max_workers=self._num_bg_threads, thread_name_prefix="fromager-bg"
            )
        )

        # Delegate resolution to BootstrapRequirementResolver
        self._resolver = bootstrap_requirement_resolver.BootstrapRequirementResolver(
            ctx=ctx,
            prev_graph=prev_graph,
            multiple_versions=multiple_versions,
            cache_wheel_server_url=self.cache_wheel_server_url,
        )
        # Push items onto the stack as we start to resolve their
        # dependencies so at the end we have a list of items that need to
        # be built in order.
        self._build_stack: list[typing.Any] = []
        self._build_requirements: set[tuple[NormalizedName, str]] = set()

        # Track requirements we've seen before so we don't resolve the
        # same dependencies over and over and so we can break cycles in
        # the dependency list. The key is the requirements spec, rather
        # than the package, in case we do have multiple rules for the same
        # package.
        self._seen_requirements: set[SeenKey] = set()

        self._build_order_filename = self.ctx.work_dir / "build-order.json"
        self._stack_filename = self.ctx.work_dir / "bootstrap-stack.json"
        logger.info("recording bootstrap stack state to %s", self._stack_filename)

        # Track failed packages in test mode (list of typed dicts for JSON export)
        self.failed_packages: list[FailureRecord] = []

        # Track failed versions in multiple_versions mode
        self._failed_versions: dict[tuple[str, str], Exception] = {}

    @property
    def resolver(self) -> bootstrap_requirement_resolver.BootstrapRequirementResolver:
        """Public accessor for the version resolver."""
        return self._resolver

    def has_failed_version(self, pkg_name: NormalizedName, version: Version) -> bool:
        """Return True if this (pkg_name, version) has previously failed resolution."""
        return (pkg_name, str(version)) in self._failed_versions

    def _resolve_and_add_top_level(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
    ) -> tuple[str, Version] | None:
        """Resolve a top-level requirement and add it to the dependency graph.

        Private method called only by ``bootstrap()``.

        This is the pre-resolution phase before recursive bootstrapping begins.
        In test mode, catches resolution errors and records them as failures.

        When multiple_versions is enabled, resolves and adds all matching versions
        to the graph, but still returns only the first (highest) version for
        backward compatibility.

        Args:
            req: The top-level requirement to resolve.

        Returns:
            Tuple of (source_url, version) if resolution succeeded, None if it
            failed in test mode.

        Raises:
            Exception: In normal mode, re-raises any resolution error.
        """
        try:
            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)
            results = self.resolve_versions(
                req=req,
                req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
                parent_req=None,
                return_all_versions=self.multiple_versions,
            )
            if self.multiple_versions:
                logger.info(f"resolved {len(results)} version(s) for {req}")

            # Add all resolved versions to the graph
            for source_url, version in results:
                logger.info("%s resolves to %s", req, version)
                self.ctx.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
                    parent_name=None,
                    parent_version=None,
                    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
                    req=req,
                    req_version=version,
                    download_url=source_url,
                    pre_built=pbi.pre_built,
                    constraint=self.ctx.constraints.get_constraint(req.name),
                )

            if not results:
                if self.multiple_versions:
                    err = RuntimeError(f"no versions found for {req}")
                    self._record_failed_version(
                        req, "unresolved", err, "no versions resolved, skipping"
                    )
                    if self.test_mode:
                        self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
                    return None
                raise RuntimeError(f"Could not resolve any versions for {req}")

            # Return first result for backward compatibility
            return results[0]
        except Exception as err:
            if self.multiple_versions:
                self._record_failed_version(req, "unresolved", err, "failed to resolve")
                if self.test_mode:
                    self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
                return None
            if not self.test_mode:
                raise
            self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
            return None

    def resolve_versions(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,
        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,
