{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_6","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc 'cat /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/caveman/SKILL.md /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/surgical-patch/SKILL.md'","aggregated_output":"---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n---\nname: surgical-patch\ndescription: Fix bugs and small behavior changes at the narrowest responsible layer. Use when regression proof, preserved surrounding behavior, and task-relevant tests matter.\n---\n\n# Surgical patch\n\nReproduce failure first when economical; otherwise capture strongest available evidence.\n\n- Trace symptom to responsible mechanism.\n- Change narrowest layer that owns incorrect behavior.\n- Preserve unrelated behavior and user changes.\n- Avoid cleanup, renaming, and abstraction outside fix.\n- Add only regression proof relevant to task.\n\nRun focused proof plus nearest affected gate. Stop when failure is fixed and regression proof passes.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

PyPI lookup (via existing sources/resolver modules)\n\n    Git URL resolution is NOT handled here - that stays in Bootstrapper\n    because it requires BuildEnvironment and build dependencies.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        ctx: context.WorkContext,\n        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,\n        multiple_versions: bool = False,\n        cache_wheel_server_url: str = \"\",\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize requirement resolver.\n\n        Args:\n            ctx: Work context with constraints and settings\n            prev_graph: Optional previous dependency graph for caching\n            multiple_versions: If ``True`` and no results are found through\n                any other approach, takes the latest candidate from the\n                cache server, ignoring the age filters.  In all other\n                cases, returns an empty list when no candidates are found.\n            cache_wheel_server_url: URL of the remote wheel cache server.\n                Used as a fallback when age filtering produces no candidates.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.ctx = ctx\n        self.prev_graph = prev_graph\n        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions\n        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url\n        # All known versions for a package, accumulated across resolution\n        # contexts.  Versions discovered via different specifiers or req_types\n        # are merged so that later lookups see the widest set.\n        # Key: (normalized_name, pre_built)\n        # Value: {version: url}\n        self._known_versions: dict[tuple[NormalizedName, bool], dict[Version, str]] = {}\n        # Requirement rules already resolved from network/graph.\n        # Key: (str(req), pre_built)\n        # Prevents redundant network calls for the same specifier.\n        self._resolved_rules: set[tuple[str, bool]] = set()\n        # Protects _known_versions and _resolved_rules for thread safety.\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def resolve(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,\n        pre_built: bool | None = None,\n        return_all_versions: bool = False,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n        \"\"\"Resolve package requirement to matching version(s).\n\n        Uses a two-step strategy:\n        1. If this requirement rule has not been resolved before, fetch\n           versions from the network (or previous graph) and extend the\n           package-level known-versions cache.\n        2. Filter all known versions for the package by the current\n           requirement specifier.\n\n        This ensures that versions discovered in one context (e.g.,\n        top-level with cooldown bypass) are visible to later lookups\n        with different specifiers for the same package.\n\n        Args:\n            req: Package requirement\n            req_type: Type of requirement\n            parent_req: Parent requirement from dependency chain\n            pre_built: Optional override to force prebuilt (True) or source (False).\n                If None (default), uses package build info to determine.\n            return_all_versions: If True, return all matching versions. If False,\n                return only the highest matching version.\n\n        Returns:\n            List of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).\n            Contains one item when return_all_versions=False, or all matching\n            versions when return_all_versions=True.\n\n        \"\"\"\n        # Determine pre_built if not specified (needed for cache key)\n        if pre_built is None:\n            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)\n            pre_built = pbi.pre_built\n\n        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)\n\n        with self._lock:\n            if rule_key not in self._resolved_rules:\n                # Rule not seen before — resolve from graph or network and\n                # extend the package-level known-versions cache.\n                self._resolve_and_extend(req, req_type, pre_built, parent_req)\n                self._resolved_rules.add(rule_key)\n            else:\n                logger.debug(f\"rule already resolved: {req}\")\n\n            # Filter all known versions by the current requirement specifier.\n            matching = self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)\n\n        if not matching:\n            return []\n        if return_all_versions:\n            return matching\n        return [matching[0]]\n\n    def get_cached_resolution(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        pre_built:   if best is not None:\n            logger.info(\"found version %s on cache server\", best[1])\n            return [best]\n        return []\n\n    def get_matching_versions(\n        self,\n days: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Set the maximum release age in days.\"\"\"\n        if days < 1:\n            raise ValueError(f\"max_release_age must be positive, got {days}\")\n        self._max_release_age = datetime.timedelta(days=days)\n\n    def enable_parallel_builds(self) -> None:\n        self._parallel_builds = True\n\n    @property\n    def wheels_build(self) -> uv_clean_cache(self, *reqs: Requirement) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Invalidate and clean uv cache for requirements\n\n        uv caches package metadata and unpacked wheels for faster dependency\n reqs:\n            raise ValueError(\"no requirements\")\n\n        extra_environ: dict[str, str] = {\"UV_CACHE_DIR\": str(self.uv_cache)}\n        cmd = [\"uv\", \"clean\", \"cache\"]\n        req_list: list[str] = sorted(set(req.name for req in reqs))\n        logger.debug(\"invalidate uv cache for %s\", req_list)\n        cmd.extend(req_list)\n        external_commands.run(cmd, mock_resolve.assert_called_once()\n        assert len(results) == 1\n        url, version = results[0]\n        assert url == \"https://files.pythonhosted.org/mypackage-2.0.tar.gz\"\n        assert version == Version(\"2.0\")\n\n\n@patch(\"fromager.resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider\")\ndef test_resolve_cache_returns_independent_lists(\n    mock_resolve: MagicMock,\n    tmp_context: WorkContext,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"resolve() returns independent list copies from the cache, not shared references.\"\"\"\n    req = Requirement(\"mypkg>=1.0\")\n    mock_resolve.return_value = [\n        (\"https://example.com/mypkg-2.0.tar.gz\", Version(\"2.0\")),\n        (\"https://example.com/mypkg-1.5.tar.gz\", Version(\"1.5\")),\n    ]\n\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context)\n\n    # First call populates cache\n    results1 = resolver.resolve(\n        req=req,\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        parent_req=None,\n        pre_built=False,\n        return_all_versions=True,\n    )\n\n    # Mutate the returned list\n    results1.append((\"https://example.com/injected.tar.gz\", Version(\"9.9\")))\n\n    # Second call should return clean cached data, unaffected by mutation\n    results2 = resolver.resolve(\n        req=req,\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        parent_req=None,\n        pre_built=False,\n        return_all_versions=True,\n    )\n\n    assert len(results2) == 2\n    assert results1 is not results2\n    # Only called once — second call used cache\n    mock_resolve.assert_called_once()\n\n\n@patch(\"fromager.resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider\")\ndef test_toplevel_version_visible_to_transitive_via_cache(\n    mock_resolve: MagicMock,\n    tmp_context: WorkContext,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Version found via top-level bypass is visible to later transitive lookups.\n\n    Simulates the architect's scenario:\n    1. Top-level A==2.0.0 resolves with cooldown bypassed → v2.0 cached\n    2. Transitive A>=1.0 resolves with cooldown enforced → only v1.5 from network\n    3. But v2.0 is already in the package-level cache, so the transitive\n       lookup returns v2.0 as the highest matching version.\n    \"\"\"\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context)\n\n    # Step 1: top-level resolves A==2.0.0 (cooldown bypassed)\n    mock_resolve.return_value = [\n        (\"https://files.test/mypkg-2.0.tar.gz\", Version(\"2.0\")),\n    ]\n    results_toplevel = resolver.resolve(\n        req=Requirement(\"mypkg==2.0\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,\n        parent_req=None,\n        pre_built=False,\n    )\n    assert results_toplevel[0][1] == Version(\"2.0\")\n    assert mock_resolve.call_count == 1\n\n    # Step 2: transitive resolves A>=1.0 (cooldown enforced, only finds v1.5)\n    mock_resolve.return_value = [\n        (\"https://files.test/mypkg-1.5.tar.gz\", Version(\"1.5\")),\n    ]\n    results_transitive = resolver.resolve(\n        req=Requirement(\"mypkg>=1.0\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        parent_req=None,\n        pre_built=False,\n    )\n    assert mock_resolve.call_count == 2\n\n    # The transitive lookup sees v2.0 from the package-level cache (found\n    # during top-level resolution) even though the transitive network call\n    # only returned v1.5.\n    assert results_transitive[0][1] == Version(\"2.0\")\n\n\n@patch(\"fromager.resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider\")\ndef test_resolve_prebuilt_after_source_uses_separate_cache(\n    mock_resolve: MagicMock,\n    tmp_context: WorkContext,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"resolve(pre_built=True) after same req resolved as source uses separate cache.\"\"\"\n    req = Requirement(\"testpkg==1.5\")\n\n    # Set up side_effect to return different results for each call\n    mock_resolve.side_effect = [\n        # First call: source resolution\n        [(\"https://files.pythonhosted.org/testpkg-1.5.tar.gz\", Version(\"1.5\"))],\n        # Second call: wheel resolution\n        [\n            (\n                \"https://files.pythonhosted.org/testpkg-1.5-py3-none-any.whl\",\n                Version(\"1.5\"),\n            )\n        ],\n    ]\n\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context)\n\n    # First call: resolve as source (explicit pre_built=False)\n    results1 = resolver.resolve(\n        req=req,\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        parent_req=None,\n        pre_built=False,\n    )\n\n    assert len(results1) == 1\n    url1, version1 = results1[0]\n    assert url1 == \"https://files.pythonhosted.org/testpkg-1.5.tar.gz\"\n    assert version1 == Version(\"1.5\")\n    assert mock_resolve.call_count == 1\n\n    # Second call: resolve same req as prebuilt (explicit pre_built=True)\n    # This should NOT return the cached source result\n    results2 = resolver.resolve(\n        req=req,\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        parent_req=None,\n        pre_built=True,\n    )\n\n    # Verify it called resolution again (not cached) because cache keys differ\n    assert mock_resolve.call_count == 2\n    assert len(results2) == 1\n    url2, version2 = results2[0]\n    assert url2 == \"https://files.pythonhosted.org/testpkg-1.5-py3-none-any.whl\"\n    assert version2 == Version(\"1.5\")\n\n\nclass TestResolveFromCacheServer:\n    \"\"\"Tests for the cache server fallback in _resolve_from_cache_server.\"\"\"\n\n    def test_returns_newest_version_from_cache(self, tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Falls back to cache server and returns only the newest version.\"\"\"\n        brr = BootstrapRequirementResolver(\n            tmp_context,\n            multiple_versions=True,\n            cache_wheel_server_url=\"http://cache.test/simple\",\n        )\n        req = Requirement(\"testpkg\")\n\n        with patch(\n            \"fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.resolver\"\n            \".find_all_matching_from_provider\",\n            return_value=[\n                (\"http://cache.test/testpkg-3.0.whl\", Version(\"3.0\")),\n                (\"http://cache.test/testpkg-2.0.whl\", Version(\"2.0\")),\n            ],\n        ):\n            result = brr._resolve_from_cache_server(req)\n\n        assert len(result) == 1\n        assert result[0][1] == Version(\"3.0\")\n\n    def test_returns_empty_when_cache_has_no_match(\n        self, tmp_context: WorkContext\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Returns empty list when cache server has nothing.\"\"\"\n        brr = BootstrapRequirementResolver(\n            tmp_context,\n            multiple_versions=True,\n            cache_wheel_server_url=\"http://cache.test/simple\",\n        )\n        req = Requirement(\"testpkg\")\n\n        with patch(\n            \"fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.resolver\"\n            \".find_all_matching_from_provider\",\n            return_value=[],\n        ):\n            result = brr._resolve_from_cache_server(req)\n\n        assert result == []\n\n    def test_returns_empty_on_exception(self, tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Returns empty list when cache server query fails.\"\"\"\n        brr = BootstrapRequirementResolver(\n            tmp_context,\n            multiple_versions=True,\n            cache_wheel_server_url=\"http://cache.test/simple\",\n        )\n        req = Requirement(\"testpkg\")\n\n        with patch(\n            \"fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.resolver\"\n            \".find_all_matching_from_provider\",\n            side_effect=RuntimeError(\"connection refused\"),\n        ):\n            result = brr._resolve_from_cache_server(req)\n\n        assert result == []\n\n    def test_resolve_uses_cache_fallback_when_age_filter_empties(\n        self, tmp_context: WorkContext\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"resolve() falls back to cache server when age filter produces empty result.\"\"\"\n        brr = BootstrapRequirementResolver(\n            tmp_context,\n            multiple_versions=True,\n            cache_wheel_server_url=\"http://cache.test/simple\",\n        )\n        req = Requirement(\"testpkg\")\n\n        with (\n            patch.object(brr, \"_resolve_from_graph\", return_value=None),\n            patch(\n                \"fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.sources.get_source_provider\",\n            ),\n            patch(\n                \"fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.resolver\"\n                \".find_all_matching_from_provider\",\n                return_value=[],\n            ) as mock_pypi,\n            patch.object(\n                brr,\n                \"_resolve_from_cache_server\",\n                return_value=[(\"http://cache.test/testpkg-1.0.whl\", Version(\"1.0\"))],\n            ) as mock_cache,\n        ):\n            result = brr.resolve(\n                req,\n                RequirementType.INSTALL,\n                parent_req=None,\n                pre_built=False,\n                return_all_versions=True,\n            )\n\n        mock_pypi.assert_called_once()\n        mock_cache.assert_called_once_with(req)\n        assert len(result) == 1\n        assert result[0][1] == Version(\"1.0\")\n\n    def test_resolve_skips_cache_fallback_in_single_version_mode(\n        self, tmp_context: WorkContext\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"resolve() does not fall back to cache server in single-version mode.\"\"\"\n        brr = BootstrapRequirementResolver(\n            tmp_context,\n            multiple_versions=False,\n            cache_wheel_server_url=\"http://cache.test/simple\",\n        )\n        req = Requirement(\"testpkg\")\n\n        with (\n            patch.object(brr, \"_resolve_from_graph\", return_value=None),\n            patch(\n                \"fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.sources.get_source_provider\",\n            ),\n            patch(\n                \"fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.resolver\"\n                \".find_all_matching_from_provider\",\n                return_value=[(\"url\", Version(\"1.0\"))],\n            ),\n            patch.object(brr, \"_resolve_from_cache_server\") as mock_cache,\n        ):\n            brr.resolve(\n                req,\n                RequirementType.INSTALL,\n                parent_req=None,\n                pre_built=False,\n            )\n\n        mock_cache.assert_not_called()\n\n    def test_resolve_skips_cache_fallback_when_no_server_url(\n        self, tmp_context: WorkContext\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"resolve() does not fall back when no cache_wheel_server_url is set.\"\"\"\n        brr = BootstrapRequirementResolver(\n            tmp_context,\n            multiple_versions=True,\n            cache_wheel_server_url=\"\",\n        )\n        req = Requirement(\"testpkg\")\n\n        with (\n            patch.object(brr, \"_resolve_from_graph\", return_value=None),\n            patch(\n                \"fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.sources.get_source_provider\",\n            ),\n            patch(\n                \"fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.resolver\"\n                \".find_all_matching_from_provider\",\n                return_value=[],\n            ),\n            patch.object(brr, \"_resolve_from_cache_server\") as mock_cache,\n        ):\n            brr.resolve(\n                req,\n                RequirementType.INSTALL,\n                parent_req=None,\n                pre_built=False,\n                return_all_versions=True,\n            )\n\n        mock_cache.assert_not_called()\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_12","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc \"cat docs/concepts/resolver-architecture.rst; sed -n '185,330p' pyproject.toml; sed -n '1,110p' src/fromager/candidate.py; sed -n '1,55p' src/fromager/requirements_file.py; sed -n '1,90p' src/fromager/packagesettings.py; sed -n '1,90p' src/fromager/commands.py; ls .venv/bin\"","aggregated_output":"Resolver Architecture\n=====================\n\nFromager resolves package versions from multiple sources using a\nprovider abstraction.  This document describes the resolution\nstrategies, filtering, and key design decisions.\n\n.. seealso::\n\n   :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.\n   :doc:`bootstrapper-architecture` covers how resolution fits into the\n   bootstrap pipeline.\n\nResolution Strategies\n---------------------\n\nDuring bootstrap, the resolver coordinator tries these sources in\npriority order and accumulates results in a thread-safe session cache:\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n   │               Resolution Priority Order               │\n   │                                                       │\n   │  1. Session cache (versions found earlier)            │\n   │          │ miss                                       │\n   │          ▼                                            │\n   │  2. Previous dependency graph (prior run)             │\n   │          │ miss                                       │\n   │          ▼                                            │\n   │  3. Network (PyPI / GitHub / GitLab)                  │\n   │     (per-package configurable)                        │\n   │          │ age filter empties result                  │\n   │          ▼                                            │\n   │  4. Cache server fallback                             │\n   │     (multiple_versions mode only)                     │\n   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n\n   Git URL requirements (top-level only) bypass this\n   chain entirely: the repo is cloned and the version\n   is extracted from package metadata.\n\nVersions discovered from any source are merged into the session cache.\nSubsequent requests for the same package skip the network entirely if\nthe cache already contains a matching version.\n\nProvider Hierarchy\n------------------\n\nAll resolution sources inherit from ``BaseProvider``, which implements\nthe resolvelib ``ExtrasProvider`` interface.  The bootstrap engine and\nCLI commands interact with providers through a common\n``find_matches()`` method.\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   BaseProvider\n   ├── PyPIProvider         (PEP 503 Simple API)\n   │   └── PyPICacheProvider  (fromager's own wheel server)\n   ├── GenericProvider      (callback-based, parses tags)\n   │   ├── GitHubTagProvider\n   │   └── GitLabTagProvider\n   └── VersionMapProvider   (pre-resolved version→URL map)\n\n.. list-table::\n   :header-rows: 1\n   :widths: 25 75\n\n   * - Provider\n     - What it queries\n   * - ``PyPIProvider``\n     - Any PEP 503 Simple API index (pypi.org, custom mirrors).\n       Filters by platform tags, Python version, and yanked status.\n   * - ``PyPICacheProvider``\n     - Subclass of ``PyPIProvider`` pointing at fromager's own wheel\n       server.  No cooldown applied.  Used as a fallback when age\n       filtering eliminates all candidates.\n   * - ``GenericProvider``\n     - Callback-based provider that pairs a version source function\n       with a configurable match function (plain parse or regex).\n       Base class for the tag providers below.\n   * - ``GitHubTagProvider``\n     - GitHub REST API for repository tags.  Versions are parsed\n       from tag names using a configurable pattern.\n   * - ``GitLabTagProvider``\n     - GitLab REST API for repository tags.  Includes upload\n       timestamps for age filtering.\n   * - ``VersionMapProvider``\n     - Wraps a pre-built ``VersionMap`` (version → URL mapping).\n       Used when versions are already known, e.g. from a prior\n       resolution or a settings-provided URL template.\n\nPer-package settings in YAML can select which provider to use and\nconfigure its parameters (index URL, tag pattern, etc.).  Override\nplugins can replace the provider entirely for a specific package via\nthe ``get_resolver_provider`` hook.\n\nVersion Filtering Window\n-------------------------\n\nTwo age-based filters can narrow the set of acceptable versions:\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   ◄── too old ──┤  acceptable window  ├── too new ──►\n\n                 │                      │\n            max_age cutoff         cooldown cutoff\n          (reject before this)   (reject after this)\n\n- **Cooldown** rejects releases that are too new.  It ensures a\n  minimum time has passed since publication, guarding against\n  problematic releases.  Configurable per package; bypassed for\n  exact version pins (``==``).\n\n- **Max age** rejects releases that are too old.  Used primarily in\n  ``multiple_versions`` mode to limit the range of versions built.\n\nWhen both are active, only versions published within the window are\nconsidered.  If all candidates are filtered out, the behavior depends\non the mode: in single-version mode a warning is logged and all\ncandidates are kept; in ``multiple_versions`` mode the cache server\nfallback is tried instead.\n\nFlat Resolution by Design\n-------------------------\n\nFromager deliberately does **not** use resolvelib's transitive\ndependency resolution.  Every provider's ``get_dependencies()`` method\nreturns an empty list.  This means resolution is a simple \"find the\nbest matching version\" operation, not a full constraint solver with\nbacktracking.\n\nTransitive dependencies are handled by the bootstrap engine's own DFS\nloop: after a package is built, its install dependencies are extracted\nfrom the wheel metadata and pushed onto the work stack as new\n``RESOLVE`` phase items.  This separation keeps the resolver stateless\nand makes each resolution call independent and thread-safe.\n\nPer-Package Configuration\n-------------------------\n\nPackage settings files (YAML) can configure the resolver for each\npackage independently: resolver type (PyPI, GitHub tags, GitLab tags,\nhook-based, or blocked), index URL, cooldown, tag pattern, and\noverride plugins.\n\nSee :doc:`package-settings` for how settings are loaded and merged.\n    \"TID252\", # Prefer absolute imports over relative imports from parent modules\n    \"UP015\",  # Unnecessary open mode parameters\n]\n\n[tool.ruff.lint.isort]\nknown-first-party = [\"fromager\"]\n\n[tool.mypy]\nmypy_path = [\"src\", \"tests\", \"e2e\"]\n# TODO: tighten type checks\ncheck_untyped_defs = true\ndisallow_incomplete_defs = true\ndisallow_untyped_defs = true\nwarn_return_any = true\n\n# TODO: remove excludes and silent follow\nfollow_imports = \"silent\"\nexclude = [\n annotations and stubs\nmodule = [\"hatchling\", \"hatchling.build\", \"license_expression\", \"pyproject_hooks\", \"requests_mock\", \"resolver\", \"spdx_tools.*\", \"stevedore\", \"wheel.*\"]\nignore_missing_imports = true\n\n[tool.basedpyright]\nreportUnannotatedClassAttribute = false\nreportUnusedCallResult = false\nreportUntypedFunctionDecorator = {args:tests}\"\ncoverage-erase = \"coverage erase\"\ncoverage-combine = \"coverage combine\"\ncoverage-report = [\"coverage combine\", \"coverage report --format=markdown | tee coverage-report-$(date install\"\npkglint = [\n  \"python -m build\",\n  \"twine check dist/*.tar.gz dist/*.whl\",\n  \"check-python-versions --only pyproject.toml,.github/workflows/test.yaml\",\n]\n# Local pre-commit hook scripts\nmergify = \"python ./e2e/mergify_lint.py\"\n\n[tool.hatch.envs.e2e]\ndescription = \"Run end-to-end tests.\"\ndependencies = [\"coverage[toml]\", \"twine\"]\nenv-vars.COVERAGE_PROCESS_START = \"{root}/pyproject.toml\"\n[tool.hatch.envs.e2e.scripts]\n# Script to create cov.pth for coverage in subprocesses\nsetup-cov = \"python e2e/setup_coverage.py\"\n# Generic script to run any command in the e2e environment\n# e.g. hatch run e2e:run ./e2e/test_bootstrap.sh\nrun = \"{args}\"\n\n[tool.hatch.envs.mypy]\ndescription = \"Python type checking with mypy.\"\nfeatures = [\"mypy\"]\n[tool.hatch.envs.mypy.scripts]\ncheck = [\n  \"mypy -p fromager\",\n  \"mypy tests/\",\n  \"mypy e2e/\",\n]\n\n[tool.hatch.envs.docs]\ndescription = \"Sphinx docs.\"\nfeatures = [\"docs\"]\n[tool.hatch.envs.docs.scripts]\nbuild = \"sphinx-build -M html docs docs/_build -j auto --keep-going {args:--fail-on-warning --fresh-env -n}\"\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\n# run tests in parallel with 3 pytest-xdist workers\naddopts = \"-n 3\"\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\nmarkers = [\n    \"network: test that need network access\",\n]\nimport dataclasses\nimport datetime\nimport logging\nimport posixpath\nimport typing\nfrom io import BytesIO\nfrom urllib.parse import urlparse\nfrom zipfile import ZipFile\n\nfrom packaging.metadata import Metadata\nfrom packaging.requirements import Requirement\nfrom packaging.utils import BuildTag, canonicalize_name\nfrom packaging.version import Version\n\nfrom .pkgmetadata.pep376 import dist_info_name\nfrom .request_session import session\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\n@dataclasses.dataclass\nclass Cooldown:\n    \"\"\"Policy for rejecting recently-published package versions.\n\n    bootstrap_time is fixed at construction so all resolutions in a single run\n    share the same cutoff.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    min_age: datetime.timedelta\n    bootstrap_time: datetime.datetime = dataclasses.field(\n        default_factory=lambda: datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)\n    )\n\n\n@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, order=True, slots=True, repr=False, kw_only=True)\nclass Candidate:\n    name: str\n    version: Version\n    url: str\n    is_sdist: bool | None = dataclasses.field(default=None)\n    extras: tuple[str, ...] = dataclasses.field(default=(), compare=False)\n    build_tag: BuildTag = dataclasses.field(default=(), compare=False)\n    has_metadata: bool = dataclasses.field(default=False, compare=False)\n    remote_tag: str | None = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False)\n    remote_commit: str | None = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False)\n    upload_time: datetime.datetime | None = dataclasses.field(\n        default=None, compare=False\n    )\n\n    _metadata: Metadata | None = dataclasses.field(\n        default=None, init=False, compare=False\n    )\n    _dependencies: list[Requirement] | None = dataclasses.field(\n        default=None, init=False, compare=False\n    )\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        # force normalized name\n        object.__setattr__(self, \"name\", canonicalize_name(self.name))\n\n    def __repr__(self) -> str:\n        if not self.extras:\n            return f\"<{self.name}=={self.version}>\"\n        return f\"<{self.name}[{','.join(self.extras)}]=={self.version}>\"\n\n    @property\n    def metadata_url(self) -> str | None:\n        \"\"\"PEP 658: metadata is available at {url}.metadata\"\"\"\n        if self.has_metadata:\n            return self.url + \".metadata\"\n        return None\n\n    @property\n    def metadata(self) -> Metadata:\n        if self._metadata is None:\n            if not self.has_metadata:\n                raise ValueError(f\"{self.url} does not have metadata\")\n            metadata = get_metadata_for_wheel(self.url, self.metadata_url)\n            object.__setattr__(self, \"_metadata\", metadata)\n        assert self._metadata\n        return self._metadata\n\n    def _get_dependencies(self) -> typing.Iterable[Requirement]:\n        deps = self.metadata.requires_dist or []\n        extras = self.extras if self.extras else [\"\"]\n\n        for r in deps:\n            if r.marker is None:\n                yield r\n            else:\n                for e in extras:\n                    if r.marker.evaluate({\"extra\": e}):\n                        yield r\n\n    @property\n    def dependencies(self) -> list[Requirement]:\n        if self._dependencies is None:\n            dependencies = list(self._get_dependencies())\n            object.__setattr__(self, \"_dependencies\", dependencies)\n        assert self._dependencies\n        return self._dependencies\n\n    @property\n    def requires_python(self) -> str | None:\n        spec = self.metadata.requires_python\n        return str(spec) if spec is not None else None\n\n\ndef get_metadata_for_wheel(\n    url: str, metadata_url: str | None = None, *, validate: bool = """Tests for bootstrap_requirement_resolver module."""

from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import resolver
from fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver import BootstrapRequirementResolver
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

# Test fixture: previous dependency graph
old_graph = DependencyGraph()

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("foo"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("foo"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
    req_version=Version("7"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("bar"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("bar"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
    req_version=Version("6"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("blah"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("blah"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
    req_version=Version("5"),
)


def test_resolve_from_graph_no_changes(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver resolves from previous graph with no changes."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Resolving new dependency that doesn't exist in graph
    assert (
        resolver._resolve_from_graph(
            req=Requirement("xyz"),
            req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
            pre_built=False,
            parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
        )
        is None
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("7"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_install_dep_upgrade(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver prefers top-level requirements over history."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement of pbr==8
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,
        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
        req=Requirement("pbr==8"),
        req_version=Version("8"),
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo - should get upgraded version from top-level
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("8"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar - constraint prevents upgrade
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah - exact version requirement
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_install_dep_downgrade(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver handles version downgrades from top-level requirements."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement of pbr<=6
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,

        req=Requirement("pbr<=6"),
        req_version=Version("6"),

    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah - exact version requirement
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]

"""Tests for the release-age cooldown policy (issue #877).

The cooldown rejects package versions published fewer than N days ago,
protecting against supply-chain attacks where a malicious version is
published and immediately pulled in by automated builds.
"""

import datetime
import logging
import pathlib
import re
import typing

import pytest
import requests_mock
import resolvelib
import yaml
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import (
    candidate,
    constraints,
    context,
    packagesettings,
    resolver,
    sources,
    wheels,
)
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

_BOOTSTRAP_TIME = datetime.datetime(2026, 3, 26, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS = datetime.timedelta(days=7)
# cutoff = 2026-03-19T00:00:00Z

# Use PEP 691 JSON format — pypi_simple reliably parses upload-time from JSON.
_PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json"

# Three versions at known ages:
#   2.0.0  uploaded 2026-03-24 →  2 days old (within cooldown)
#   1.3.2  uploaded 2026-03-15 → 11 days old (outside cooldown)
#   1.2.2  uploaded 2026-01-01 → 84 days old (outside cooldown)
_cooldown_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-15T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "ccc"},
            "upload-time": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_all_recent_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-25T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_COOLDOWN = candidate.Cooldown(
    min_age=_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS,
    bootstrap_time=_BOOTSTRAP_TIME,
)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clear_resolver_cache() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:
    """Clear the class-level resolver cache before each test.

    BaseProvider.resolver_cache is a ClassVar that persists across test
    instances. Without clearing it, candidates fetched in one test are reused
    by subsequent tests, bypassing mocked HTTP responses and producing
    incorrect results.
    """
    resolver.BaseProvider.clear_cache()
    resolver.BaseProvider._cooldown_unsupported_warned.clear()
    yield


def test_cooldown_filters_recent_version(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Versions within the cooldown window are skipped; older ones are selected."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
            result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        # 2.0.0 is 2 days old (within cooldown); 1.3.2 is 11 days old (outside).
        assert str(candidate.version) == "1.3.2"
        # 2.0.0 should be logged as blocked; 1.3.2 should not appear in the summary.
        assert "cooldown blocked 1 version(s): 2.0.0" in caplog.text


def test_cooldown_disabled_selects_latest() -> None:
    """Without a cooldown the resolver selects the latest version as normal."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=None)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        assert str(candidate.version) == "2.0.0"


def test_cooldown_all_blocked_raises_informative_error() -> None:
    """When all candidates are within the cooldown window the error says so."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_all_recent_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())

        with pytest.raises(resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException) as exc_info:
            rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        msg = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "2 candidate(s)" in msg
        assert "published within the last 7 days (release-age cooldown" in msg


def test_cooldown_rejects_candidate_without_upload_time(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """A candidate with no upload_time is rejected when a cooldown is active (fail closed)."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    candidate = resolver.Candidate(
        name="test-pkg",
        version=Version("1.0.0"),
        url="https://example.com/test-pkg-1.0.0.tar.gz",
        upload_time=None,
    )
    provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(cooldown=_COOLDOWN)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
        result = provider.is_blocked_by_cooldown(candidate)

    assert result is True
    assert "upload_time unknown" in caplog.text
    assert "1.0.0" in caplog.text
